verses.text: 1:1The word of God that came upon Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests, who lived in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin,
1:2which became God’s word to him in the days of Josiah son of Amos, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.
1:3It also came in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, until Jerusalem’s captivity in the fifth month.
1:4The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
1:5Before I formed you in the belly, I know you; before you came out of the womb, I have consecrated you. I have appointed you a prophet to nations. [1]
1:6I said, O Master Lord! Behold, I do not know how to speak, because I am young.
1:7The Lord said to me, Do not say, I am young, because you will go to everyone to whom I send you, and you will speak according to everything I command you.
1:8Do not fear them, because I am with you to rescue you, says the Lord.
1:9The Lord stretched out His hand toward me and touched my mouth. The Lord said to me, Behold, I have put My words into your mouth.
1:10Behold, today I have appointed you over nations and kingdoms, to uproot, demolish, destroy, build and plant.
1:11The Lord’s word came to me, saying, What do you see, Jeremiah? I said, A nut-wood staff.
1:12The Lord said to me, You have seen well, because I am watchful over My words to perform them.
1:13The Lord’s word came to me a second time, saying, What do you see? I said, A cauldron heated from beneath, its face away from the north.
1:14The Lord said to me, From the north calamities will be kindled upon all who inhabit the land.

1:15Because behold, I am summoning all the kingdoms from the north of the land, says the Lord. They will come and each set his throne at the forecourts of Jerusalem’s gates, against all her surrounding walls and against all Judah’s cities.
1:16I will speak to them with judgment concerning all their evil, because they abandoned Me, sacrificed to foreign gods and bowed down to the works of their hands.
1:17But you, gird your waist, rise and tell them everything I command you. Do not fear them or be terrified before them, because I am with you to rescue you, says the Lord.
1:18Behold, on this day I have made you like a fortified city and like a strong bronze wall against all Judah’s kings, its rulers and the people of the land,
1:19and they will fight you, but they will certainly not prevail against you, because I am with you to rescue you, said the Lord.

verses.text: 2:2And He said, Thus says the Lord: I remembered the mercy of your youth and the love of your completion, when you followed the Holy One of Israel, says the Lord.
2:3Israel is holy. To the Lord he is the first of His produce. All who devour him will offend; calamities will come upon them, declares the Lord.
2:4Hear the Lord’s word, house of Jacob and every clan of the house of Israel.
2:5Thus says the Lord: What offense did your fathers find in Me, that they withdrew far from Me, followed futile things and became futile?

2:6They did not say, Where is the Lord who brought us up from Egypt’s land, who guided us in the wilderness, in a boundless and impassable land, a waterless and fruitless land, a land through which nothing passed and where no human being lived?
2:7I brought you into Carmel to eat its fruits and good things, but you entered and polluted My land and made My inheritance an abomination.
2:8The priests did not say, Where is the Lord? Those holding to the law did not know Me; the shepherds acted ungodly toward Me; the prophets prophesied by Baal and followed what is useless.
2:9Therefore I will still enter judgment with you, says the Lord, and with your children’s children I will enter judgment.
2:10Cross over to the islands of Kittim and see; send to Kedar and consider carefully. See whether such things have happened.
2:11Will nations exchange their gods, though these are not gods? But My people exchanged their glory, from which they will not benefit.
2:12Heaven was astonished at this and shuddered exceedingly, says the Lord.
2:13For My people did two evil things: they abandoned Me, a spring of water of life, and dug broken cisterns for themselves that will not be able to hold water. [1]
2:14Is Israel a slave, or is he house-born? Why has he become spoil?
2:15Lions roared over him and raised their voice. They made his land a wilderness, and his cities were demolished so that none inhabited them.
2:16The sons of Memphis and Tahpanhes knew you and mocked you.
2:17Has abandoning Me not brought these things upon you? says the Lord your God.
2:18Now what do you have to do with Egypt’s road, to drink Gihon’s water? And what do you have to do with the Assyrians’ road, to drink river waters?
2:19Your apostasy will discipline you, and your evil will rebuke you. Know and see that abandoning Me is bitter for you, says the Lord your God; and I took no pleasure in you, says the Lord your God.

2:20For long ago you shattered your yoke and tore apart your bonds, and said, I will not be enslaved, but I will go upon every high hill and beneath every shady tree; there I will abandon myself to my prostitution.
2:21But I planted you as a fruitful vine, wholly genuine. How have you changed into bitterness, you foreign vine?
2:22Even if you wash with natron and multiply cleansing herb for yourself, you remain stained in your injustices before Me, says the Lord.
2:23How will you say, I was not polluted and did not follow Baal? See your ways in the burial ground and know what you did. Late her voice wailed; her ways

2:24she broadened upon wilderness waters. In her soul’s desires she was carried by the wind; she was handed over. Who will turn her back? All who seek her will not toil; in her humiliation they will find her.
2:25Turn your foot from a rough road and your throat from thirst. But she said, I will be strong, because she had loved strangers and went after them.
2:26As a thief is ashamed when caught, so the sons of Israel will be ashamed: they, their kings, their rulers, their priests and their prophets.
2:27They said to wood, You are my father, and to stone, You gave birth to me. They turned their backs toward Me, not their faces; and in the time of their calamities they will say, Rise and save us!

2:28Where are your gods that you made for yourself? Will they rise and save you in the time of your affliction? For your gods were as numerous as your cities, Judah, and according to the number of Jerusalem’s streets they sacrificed to Baal.
2:29Why do you speak to Me? All of you acted ungodly, and all of you acted lawlessly against Me, says the Lord.
2:30In vain I struck your children; you accepted no discipline. A sword devoured your prophets like a destroying lion, and you did not fear.
2:31Hear the Lord’s word. Thus says the Lord: Have I become a wilderness to Israel, or a land left barren? Why did My people say, We will not be ruled, and we will come to Thee no more?
2:32Will a bride forget her adornment, or a virgin her breastband? Yet My people forgot Me for days beyond counting.
2:33What good practice will you still pursue in your ways to seek love? Not so; you too acted wickedly to pollute your ways.
2:34Even on your hands was found the blood of innocent lives. I did not find them in break-ins, but at every oak.
2:35And you said, I am innocent; let His fury turn away from me. Behold, I enter judgment with you because you say, I did not sin.
2:36Why did you show such contempt by repeating your ways? You will also be put to shame by Egypt, as you were put to shame by Assyria.
2:37For from here too you will go out with your hands on your head, because the Lord rejected your hope, and you will not prosper in it.

verses.text: 3:1If a man sends his wife away, and she leaves him and becomes another man’s, surely she will not return to him again? Would not that woman be utterly polluted? And you prostituted yourself with many shepherds—and were you returning to Me? says the Lord.
3:2Lift your eyes straight ahead and see: where have you not been defiled? You sat for them on the roads like a solitary crow, and polluted the land with your prostitution and your evils.
3:3You had many shepherds as a stumbling block for yourself. You had a prostitute’s appearance; you were shameless toward everyone.
3:4Did you not call Me a household, a father and the leader of your virginity?
3:5Will He remain for ever, or will it be guarded always? Behold, you spoke and did these evil things and were able.
3:6The Lord said to me in the days of King Josiah, You saw what the dwelling of Israel did to Me. They went upon every high mountain and beneath every wooded tree and prostituted themselves there.
3:7After she prostituted herself in all these ways, I said, Return to Me. But she did not return, and faithless Judah saw her faithlessness.

3:8I saw that, concerning all the things in which the dwelling of Israel was caught committing adultery, I sent her away and gave a certificate of divorce into her hands. Yet faithless Judah did not fear; she too went and prostituted herself.
3:9Her prostitution came to be regarded as nothing, and she committed adultery with wood and stone.
3:10In all these things faithless Judah did not return to Me with her whole heart, but in falsehood.
3:11The Lord said to me, Israel has justified himself in comparison with faithless Judah.

3:12Go and read these words toward the north: Return to Me, dwelling of Israel, says the Lord. I will not set My face firmly against you, because I am merciful, says the Lord, and I will not be angry with you for ever.
3:13Only recognize your injustice: you acted ungodly toward the Lord your God and spread your ways to strangers beneath every wooded tree, but you did not obey My voice, says the Lord.
3:14Return, children who have withdrawn, says the Lord, because I will rule over you. I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you into Zion,
3:15and I will give you shepherds according to My heart, and they will shepherd you, shepherding with knowledge.

3:16When you multiply and increase upon the land in those days, says the Lord, they will no longer say, The ark of the covenant of the Holy One of Israel. It will not come to mind, be named or be attended to, and it will not be made again.
3:17In those days and at that time they will call Jerusalem the Lord’s throne, and all the nations will gather to her. They will no longer follow the thoughts of their evil heart.
3:18In those days the house of Judah will join the house of Israel, and together they will come from the northern land and from all the regions to the land I gave their fathers as an inheritance.

3:19And I said, May it be, Lord! For I will place you among children and give you a chosen land, an inheritance of God Almighty of nations. I said, You will call Me Father and will not turn away from Me.
3:20But as a woman deals faithlessly with the one living with her, so the house of Israel dealt faithlessly with Me, says the Lord.
3:21A voice was heard from lips, the weeping and supplication of Israel’s children, because they acted unjustly in their ways and forgot their holy God.
3:22Return, returning children, and I will heal your fractures. Behold, we will be Thy servants, because Thou art the Lord our God.
3:23Truly the hills and the power of the mountains were false; but through the Lord our God is Israel’s salvation.
3:24Shame consumed our fathers’ labors from our youth: their sheep and calves, their sons and daughters.
3:25We lay down in our shame, and our dishonor covered us, because we sinned before our God, we and our fathers, from our youth until this day, and did not obey the voice of the Lord our God.

verses.text: 4:1If Israel returns, says the Lord, he will return to Me; if he removes his abominations from his mouth and shows reverence before Me,
4:2and swears, ‘The Lord lives,’ with truth and in judgment and righteousness, then nations will bless in her, and in Him they will praise God in Jerusalem.
4:3For thus says the Lord to the men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem: Break up fallow ground for yourselves, and do not sow among thorns.

4:4Be circumcised to your God, and circumcise your hardness of heart, men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem, lest My fury come out like fire and burn, and there be no one to extinguish it because of the evil of your practices.
4:5Announce in Judah, and let it be heard in Jerusalem; say: Signal with a trumpet over the land, and cry loudly! Say: Gather, and let us enter the walled cities!
4:6Take up and flee to Zion; hurry, do not stand still, for I am bringing evils from the north and great crushing.
4:7A lion has gone up from his enclosure; destroying nations, he has set out and left his place to make the land a desolation, and cities will be demolished so that they are not inhabited.
4:8For these things, gird yourselves with sackcloth, beat yourselves in mourning and wail, because the Lord’s fury has not turned away from you.
4:9And it will be on that day, says the Lord: the king’s heart and the rulers’ heart will perish, and the priests will be beside themselves and the prophets astonished.
4:10And I said: O Master, Lord, surely Thou hast indeed deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You will have peace,’ and behold, the sword has reached to their soul!
4:11At that time they will say to this people and Jerusalem: A spirit of wandering in the wilderness; the daughter of My people’s way is not toward purity or holiness.
4:12A spirit of filling will come to Me; but now I speak judgments against them.
4:13Behold, he will come up like a cloud, and his chariots like a storm; his horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, because we suffer misery!
4:14Wash your heart clean of evil, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will the schemes of your troubles exist within you?
4:15For the voice of one announcing will come from Dan, and trouble will be heard from Mount Ephraim.
4:16Remind the nations: Behold, they have come! Announce in Jerusalem: Bands come from a distant land and have raised their voice against the cities of Judah.
4:17Like those guarding a field they came against her all around, because you neglected Me, says the Lord.
4:18Your ways and your practices have done these things to you. This is your evil: it is bitter; it has reached to your heart.
4:19My belly, my belly, I am in pain, and the senses of my heart! My soul rages, my heart is torn; I will not be silent, because my soul heard the sound of a trumpet, a cry of war.
4:20It calls out misery and crushing, because the whole land has suffered misery; suddenly the tent has suffered misery, and my tent coverings have been torn apart.
4:21How long will I see people fleeing while hearing the sound of trumpets?
4:22For the leaders of My people did not know Me; they are foolish sons and not discerning. They are wise at doing evil, but did not learn to do well.
4:23I looked upon the earth, and behold, nothing; and into heaven, and its lights were not there.
4:24I saw the mountains, and they were trembling, and all the hills were being shaken.
4:25I looked, and behold, there was no human, and all the birds of heaven were terrified.
4:26I saw, and behold, Carmel was a wilderness, and all the cities were burned with fire before the Lord, and they vanished before His furious anger.
4:27Thus says the Lord: The whole land will be a wilderness, but I will certainly not make a complete end.
4:28For these things let the earth mourn and let heaven above grow dark, because I have spoken and will not change My mind; I have set Myself in motion and will not turn back from it.
4:29At the sound of a horseman and a drawn bow the whole countryside withdrew; they entered caves and hid in groves and climbed onto the rocks. Every city was abandoned; no human dwells in them.

4:30And you, what will you do if you put on scarlet and adorn yourself with golden ornaments, and if you paint your eyes with antimony? Your adornment is in vain; your lovers have rejected you; they seek your soul.

4:31For I heard a voice like a woman in labor, your groaning like one giving birth for the first time, the voice of the daughter of Zion. She will grow faint and let her hands fall: Woe to me, because my soul fails over those killed!

verses.text: 5:1Run through Jerusalem’s streets and see and learn, and search her squares: if you find a man, if there is one doing justice and seeking faithfulness, then I will be merciful to them, says the Lord.
5:2They say, ‘The Lord lives’; do they not therefore swear on falsehoods?

5:3Lord, Thine eyes are toward faithfulness. Thou didst scourge them, and they did not suffer; Thou broughtest them to an end, and they would not accept instruction. They hardened their faces beyond rock and would not return.
5:4And I said: Perhaps they are poor, because they had no ability, because they did not know the Lord’s way and God’s judgment.
5:5I will go to the prosperous and speak to them, for they recognized the Lord’s way and God’s judgment. And behold, with one accord they broke the yoke and tore the bonds.

5:6Therefore a lion from the woodland struck them, and a wolf destroyed them as far as the houses, and a leopard kept watch over their cities. All who leave them will be hunted, because they multiplied their impieties and grew strong in their turnings away.

5:7For which of these things should I be merciful to you? Your sons abandoned Me and swore by those who are not gods. And I fed them fully, and they committed adultery and lodged in prostitutes’ houses.
5:8They became horses mad for mares; each neighed after his neighbor’s wife.
5:9Shall I not visit for these things? says the Lord. Or will not My soul take vengeance on such a nation?
5:10Go up against her battlements and tear them down, but do not make a complete end. Leave her supports, because they belong to the Lord.
5:11For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have utterly rejected Me, says the Lord.
5:12They lied to their own Lord and said: These things are not so; evils will not come upon us, and we will not see sword or famine.
5:13Our prophets became wind, and the Lord’s word was not in them. Thus it will be for them.
5:14Therefore thus says the Lord Almighty: Because you spoke this utterance, behold, I have made My words fire in your mouth, and this people wood, and it will devour them.
5:15Behold, I am bringing a nation upon you from far away, house of Israel, says the Lord, a nation whose language’s sound you will not understand.
5:16All are strong,

5:17and they will devour your harvest and your bread, and devour your sons and daughters, and devour your sheep and calves, and devour your vineyards and fig orchards and olive groves; and with a sword they will thresh your fortified cities, in which you have trusted.
5:18And it will be in those days, says the Lord your God: I will certainly not bring you to a complete end.

5:19And when you say, ‘For what reason has the Lord our God done all these things to us?’ you will say to them: Because you served foreign gods in your land, so you will serve foreigners in a land not yours.
5:20Announce these things to the house of Jacob, and let it be heard in Judah.
5:21Hear these things now, foolish and senseless people: they have eyes and do not see; they have ears and do not hear.

5:22Will you not fear Me? says the Lord. Or will you not show reverence before Me, who appointed sand as the sea’s boundary, an eternal command it will not cross? It will be stirred and will not prevail, and its waves will roar, and it will not cross it.
5:23But this people acquired an unheeding and disobedient heart, and they turned aside and went away.
5:24And they did not say in their heart: Let us fear the Lord our God, who gives us early and late rain at the time of fulfillment of the harvest’s command, and He kept it for us.
5:25Your lawless acts turned these things aside, and your sins removed good things from you.
5:26For impious people were found among My people, and they set traps to destroy men and were catching them.
5:27Like a set trap full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit; therefore they became great and rich.
5:28And they transgressed judgment; they did not judge an orphan’s case, and they were not judging a widow’s case.
5:29Shall I not visit for these things? says the Lord. Or will not My soul take vengeance on such a nation?
5:30Astonishment and horrifying things happened upon the land:
5:31The prophets prophesy unjust things, and the priests applauded with their hands, and My people loved it so. And what will you do after these things?

verses.text: 6:1Take courage, sons of Benjamin, from within Jerusalem, and signal with a trumpet in Tekoa, and raise a sign above Beth-haccherem, because evils have looked out from the north, and great crushing is taking place,
6:2and your height will be taken away, daughter of Zion.
6:3Shepherds and their flocks will come to her, and they will pitch tents against her all around, and each will shepherd with his own hand.
6:4Prepare yourselves for war against her! Rise, and let us go up against her at noon! Woe to us, because the day has declined, because evening’s shadows are failing!
6:5Rise, and let us go up in the night and destroy her foundations!
6:6For thus says the Lord: Cut down her trees; pour out a force upon Jerusalem. O false city, all oppression is within her!
6:7As a cistern cools water, so her evil cools; impiety and misery will be heard in her, continually before her. With pain and scourging
6:8you will be instructed, Jerusalem, lest My soul depart from you, lest I make you an impassable land that will not be inhabited.
6:9For thus says the Lord: Glean, glean Israel’s remnants like a vine; turn back like the grape-gatherer to his basket.

6:10To whom shall I speak and testify, and he will hear? Behold, their ears are uncircumcised, and they cannot hear. Behold, the Lord’s utterance became a reproach to them; they certainly will not wish to hear it.

6:11And I filled up My fury and held back and did not bring them to an end. I will pour it upon little children outside and upon a gathering of young men together, because man and woman will be seized, the elder with one full of days.
6:12And their houses will be transferred to others, fields and their wives together, because I will stretch out My hand against those dwelling in this land, says the Lord.
6:13For from their small to their great, all have carried out lawless deeds; from priest to false prophet, all have done false things.
6:14And they treated My people’s fracture with contempt, saying, ‘Peace, peace’; and where is peace?

6:15They were put to shame because they failed, and even so they were not at all ashamed and did not recognize their dishonor. Therefore they will fall in their fall, and at the time of their visitation they will perish, said the Lord.

6:16Thus says the Lord: Stand upon the roads and see, and ask for the Lord’s eternal paths and see which is the good way, and walk in it, and you will find purification for your souls. And they said, ‘We will not go.’ [1]
6:17I have appointed watchers over you: Hear the trumpet’s sound! And they said, ‘We will not hear.’
6:18Therefore the nations heard, and those shepherding their flocks.
6:19Hear, earth! Behold, I am bringing evils upon this people, the fruit of their turning away, because they did not attend to My words and rejected My law.
6:20Why do you bring Me frankincense from Sheba and cinnamon from a distant land? Your whole burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices did not please Me.
6:21Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am placing weakness upon this people, and fathers and sons together will become weak in it; neighbor and his neighbor will perish.
6:22Thus says the Lord: Behold, a people comes from the north, and nations will be roused from the earth’s extremity.
6:23They will grasp bow and spear; it is ruthless and will show no mercy. Its voice is like a surging sea; on horses and chariots it will draw up like fire for war against you, daughter of Zion.
6:24We heard the report of them; our hands were paralyzed. Affliction seized us, labor pains like a woman giving birth.
6:25Do not go out into a field or walk on the roads, because the enemies’ sword dwells all around.
6:26Daughter of My people, gird yourself with sackcloth; sprinkle yourself with ashes. Make mourning for yourself for a beloved one, a pitiful lament, because misery will suddenly come upon you.
6:27I have made you a tester among tested peoples, and you will know Me when I test their way.
6:28All are unheeding, walking crookedly, bronze and iron; all are corrupted.
6:29The bellows failed from the fire; the lead failed. In vain the silversmith works silver; their wickedness was not melted away.
6:30Call them rejected silver, because the Lord rejected them.

verses.text: 7:2Hear the Lord’s word, all Judea!
7:3Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Correct your ways and your practices, and I will settle you in this place.
7:4Do not put your confidence in yourselves on false words, because they will not benefit you at all when they say, ‘The Lord’s temple, the Lord’s temple it is.’
7:5For if you truly correct your ways and practices and truly execute judgment between a man and his neighbor,
7:6and do not oppress a newcomer, orphan, or widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow foreign gods to your own harm,
7:7then I will settle you in this place, in the land I gave your fathers, from age to age.
7:8But if you have trusted false words from which you will receive no benefit,
7:9and murder and commit adultery and steal and swear unjustly, and you burned incense to Baal and followed foreign gods whom you do not know, to your own harm,
7:10and you came and stood before Me in the house over which My name has been called and said, ‘We have kept away, so as not to do all these abominations,’
7:11is My house, over which My name has been called there, a robbers’ cave before you? And behold, I have seen, says the Lord.
7:12For go to My place in Shiloh, where I formerly made My name dwell, and see what I did to it because of the evil of My people Israel.
7:13And now, because you did all these works, and I spoke to you and you did not hear Me, and I called you and you did not answer,
7:14I will also do to this house over which My name has been called, in which you have trusted, and to the place I gave you and your fathers, as I did to Shiloh.
7:15And I will throw you away from My presence, as I threw away your brothers, all Ephraim’s offspring.
7:16And you, do not pray for this people, and do not ask that they receive mercy, and do not pray or approach Me on their behalf, because I will not listen.
7:17Do you not see what they are doing in Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s streets?
7:18Their sons gather wood, and their fathers burn a fire, and their women work dough to make cakes for heaven’s host; and they poured drink offerings to foreign gods to provoke Me to anger.
7:19Is it Me they provoke to anger? says the Lord. Is it not themselves, so that their faces are put to shame?

7:20Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, My wrath and fury are poured upon this place, upon the people and the livestock, upon every tree of their field and all the earth’s produce; and it will burn and not be extinguished.
7:21Thus says the Lord: Gather your whole burnt offerings with your sacrifices, and eat meat!
7:22For I did not speak to your fathers or command them on the day I brought them up from Egypt’s land concerning whole burnt offerings and sacrifice.
7:23But this utterance I commanded them, saying: Hear My voice, and I will be your God and you will be My people; and walk in all My ways that I command you, so that it may be well with you.
7:24And they did not hear Me, and their ear did not attend, but they walked in the thoughts of their evil heart and went backward rather than forward.
7:25From the day their fathers left Egypt’s land until this day, I sent out to you all My servants the prophets by day and at dawn, and I sent them.
7:26And they did not hear Me, and their ear did not attend, and they hardened their neck beyond their fathers.
7:27–28And you will say this word to them: This is the nation that did not hear the Lord’s voice or accept instruction; faithfulness failed from their mouth.
7:29Shear your head and cast it away, and take up a lament on your lips, because the Lord rejected and thrust away the generation doing these things.
7:30For Judah’s sons did evil before Me, says the Lord; they set their abominations in the house over which My name has been called, to defile it.
7:31And they built Topheth’s altar, which is in the ravine of the son of Hinnom, to burn up their sons and daughters in fire, which I did not command them and did not conceive in My heart.

7:32Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say Topheth’s Altar or Ravine of the Son of Hinnom, but Ravine of the Slain; and they will bury in Topheth because there is no space.
7:33And this people’s dead will be food for heaven’s birds and the earth’s wild beasts, and there will be no one to drive them off.

7:34And I will stop the sound of those rejoicing and the sound of those glad, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride, from Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s thoroughfares, because the whole land will become a desolation.

verses.text: 8:1At that time, says the Lord, they will bring the bones of Judah’s kings and the bones of its rulers and the bones of the priests and the bones of the prophets and the bones of those dwelling in Jerusalem out of their tombs,

8:2and expose them to cool before the sun and moon and all the stars and all heaven’s host, which they loved and served and followed and clung to and bowed down to. They will not be mourned or buried, and they will be an example upon the earth’s surface,
8:3because they chose death rather than life, and for all the remnants left from that generation in every place where I drive them away.
8:4For thus says the Lord: Does one who falls not rise? Or does one who turns away not return?
8:5Why has this people of Mine turned away with a shameless turning away, and been held fast in their own choice, and been unwilling to return?
8:6Give ear now and hear: they will not speak thus; there is no person repenting of his evil, saying, ‘What have I done?’ The runner ceased from his course like a sweating horse in its neighing.
8:7Even the stork in heaven knew her time; turtledove and swallow, field sparrows, kept the times of their coming, but My people did not know the Lord’s judgments.
8:8How will you say, ‘We are wise, and the Lord’s law is with us’? A false reed-pen came to be in vain for scribes.
8:9The wise were ashamed and terrified and captured, because they rejected the Lord’s word. What wisdom is in them?
8:10Therefore I will give their wives to others and their fields to inheritors,
8:13and they will gather their produce, says the Lord. There is no grape on the vines and no figs on the fig trees, and the leaves have fallen.
8:14Why are we sitting? Gather, and let us enter the fortified cities and be cast away, because God cast us away and made us drink gall-water, because we sinned before Him.
8:15We gathered for peace, and there were no good things; for a time of healing, and behold, haste!

8:16From Dan we will hear the shrill sound of his horses; at the sound of the neighing of his riding horses the whole earth shook. And he will come and devour the earth and its fullness, a city and those dwelling in it.
8:17Because behold, I am sending out among you deadly snakes that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you.
8:18Incurable things, with pain, while your heart is bewildered.

8:19Behold, the crying voice of the daughter of My people from a distant land: ‘Is the Lord not in Zion? Is a King not there?’ Why did they provoke Me with their carved things and foreign futile things?
8:20Summer passed, harvest went by, and we were not delivered.
8:21At the crushing of the daughter of My people I was darkened; in bewilderment, pains like a woman giving birth overpowered me.
8:22Is there no resin in Gilead, or is there no physician there? Why did healing not rise for the daughter of My people?
8:23Who will give my head water and my eyes a fountain of tears, and I will weep day and night for this people of Mine, for the wounded of the daughter of My people?

verses.text: 9:1Who would give me a remote station in the wilderness, and I will leave my people and go away from them? For all commit adultery, an assembly of those rejecting faithfulness.
9:2And they stretched their tongue like a bow; falsehood and not faithfulness grew strong upon the earth, because they went from evils to evils and did not know Me.
9:3Each of you, guard against his neighbor, and do not put trust in their brothers, because every brother will trip with the heel, and every friend will walk deceitfully.
9:4Each will mock his friend; they certainly will not speak truth. Their tongue has learned to speak false things; they did wrong and did not cease turning back.
9:5Interest upon interest, deceit upon deceit: they were unwilling to know Me.
9:6Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will put them through fire and test them, because I will act on account of the evil of the daughter of My people.
9:7Their tongue is a wounding missile; the utterances of their mouth are deceitful. One speaks peaceful things to his neighbor, and within himself he holds enmity.
9:8Shall I not visit for these things? says the Lord. Or will not My soul take vengeance on such a people?

9:9Take up mourning for the mountains and a dirge for the wilderness paths, because they failed for lack of people. They did not hear the sound of possessions; from heaven’s birds to livestock, they were displaced and went away.
9:10And I will give Jerusalem over to deportation and as a dwelling of dragons, and make Judah’s cities disappear, so that they are not inhabited.

9:11Who is the discerning person? Let him understand this; and the one to whom the word of the Lord’s mouth comes, let him announce it to you: for what reason did the land perish, kindled like a wilderness so that no one passes through it?
9:12And the Lord said to me: Because they abandoned My law that I set before them and did not hear My voice,
9:13but walked after the things pleasing to their evil heart and after the idols that their fathers taught them,
9:14therefore thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Behold, I will feed them distresses and make them drink gall-water,
9:15and I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their fathers knew, and send the sword upon them until I consume them by it.
9:16Thus says the Lord: Call the women who lament, and let them come; send for the skilled women, and let them speak,
9:17and let them take up a dirge over you; let your eyes bring down tears, and let your eyelids flow with water.
9:18For a voice of lament was heard in Zion: How we suffered misery and were greatly ashamed, because we abandoned the land and threw away our dwellings!
9:19Hear God’s word now, women, and let your ears receive His mouth’s words; teach your daughters lament, and each woman her neighbor a dirge.
9:20For death climbed through your windows and entered your land, to wipe out little children outside and young men from the squares.
9:21And people’s dead will become an example on the surface of your land’s plain, and like grass behind one reaping, and there will be no one gathering.
9:22Thus says the Lord: Let no wise man boast in his wisdom, let no strong man boast in his strength, and let no rich man boast in his wealth, [1]
9:23but let whoever boasts boast in this: understanding and knowing that I am the Lord, doing mercy and judgment and righteousness upon the earth, because in these is My will, says the Lord.
9:24Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will visit all who have been circumcised in their foreskins:

9:25Egypt and Judea and Edom and the sons of Ammon and the sons of Moab and everyone who clips the hair around his face, those dwelling in the wilderness; because all the nations are uncircumcised in flesh, and all Israel’s house are uncircumcised in their hearts.

verses.text: 10:1Hear the Lord’s word that He spoke concerning you, house of Israel.
10:2Thus says the Lord: Do not learn according to the nations’ ways, and do not fear heaven’s signs, because they fear them before their faces.
10:3For the nations’ customs are futile: it is wood cut from the woodland, a carpenter’s work and a cast object.
10:4They are adorned with silver and gold; with hammers and nails they fastened them, and they will not move.
10:5They must be lifted and carried, because they will not take a step. Do not fear them, because they certainly will not do evil, and no good is in them.
10:9It is worked silver; they will not walk. Applied silver will come from Tarshish, gold from Mophaz, and the goldsmiths’ hand; all are artisans’ works. They will dress them in blue and purple.
10:11This is what you will say to them: Gods who did not make heaven and earth, let them perish from the earth and from beneath this heaven.
10:12The Lord who made the earth by His strength, who set the inhabited world upright by His wisdom, also stretched out heaven by His understanding,
10:13and an abundance of water in heaven; and He brought clouds up from the earth’s extremity, made lightning for rain, and brought light out of His treasuries.
10:14Every human became foolish, without knowledge; every goldsmith was put to shame at his carved things, because they cast false things; there is no spirit in them.
10:15They are futile, mocked works; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
10:16Jacob’s portion is not such as this, because the One who formed everything is himself his inheritance; Lord is His name.
10:17He gathered your possessions from outside, you who dwell among chosen ones.
10:18For thus says the Lord: Behold, I am tripping those dwelling in this land with affliction, so that your wound may be found.
10:19Woe for your crushing! Your wound is painful. And I said: Truly this is my wound, and it has seized me.
10:20My tent suffered misery and perished, and all my tent coverings were torn apart. My sons and my sheep are no more; there is no longer a place for my tent, a place for my coverings.
10:21For the shepherds acted foolishly and did not seek the Lord; therefore all the pasture did not perceive, and they were scattered.
10:22A sound of a report—behold, it comes! And a great shaking from the northern land, to lay Judah’s cities waste and make them a resting place for ostriches.
10:23I know, Lord, that a human’s way does not belong to him, nor will a man go and make his course straight.
10:24Instruct us, Lord, but with judgment and not in fury, so that Thou dost not make us few.
10:25Pour Thy fury upon nations who do not know Thee and upon generations who did not call on Thy name, because they devoured Jacob and consumed him and made his pasture desolate.

verses.text: 11:1The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah, saying:
11:2Hear the words of this covenant. And you will speak to the men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem,
11:3and you will say to them: Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Cursed is the person who will not hear the words of this covenant,

11:4which I commanded your fathers on the day I brought them up from Egypt’s land, from the iron furnace, saying: Hear My voice and do everything I command you, and you will be My people and I will be your God,
11:5so that I may establish My oath that I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as on this day. And I answered and said: May it be, Lord.
11:6And the Lord said to me: Read these words in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem, saying: Hear the words of this covenant and do them.
11:8And they did not do them.
11:9And the Lord said to me: A conspiracy was found among Judah’s men and those dwelling in Jerusalem.

11:10They returned to the injustices of their earlier fathers, who would not listen to My words; and behold, they walk after foreign gods to serve them. And the house of Israel and the house of Judah shattered My covenant that I established with their fathers.
11:11Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing evils upon this people from which they will not be able to escape; and they will cry to Me, and I will not listen to them.
11:12And Judah’s cities and those dwelling in Jerusalem will go and cry to the gods to whom they burn incense. Will those gods save them in the time of their evils?
11:13For your gods were according to the number of your cities, Judah; and according to the number of Jerusalem’s exits you set up altars to burn incense to Baal.
11:14And you, do not pray for this people or petition for them with supplication and prayer, because I will not listen when they call upon Me, in their time of affliction.
11:15Why has the beloved woman committed an abomination in My house? Will prayers and holy meats remove your evils from you, or will you escape by these?

11:16The Lord called your name a beautiful olive tree, well-shaded in appearance. At the sound of its pruning, fire was kindled upon it; great is the affliction upon you, and its branches became useless.

11:17And the Lord who planted you spoke evils against you in return for the evil of the house of Israel and the house of Judah, because they acted for themselves to provoke Me by burning incense to Baal.
11:18Lord, make it known to me, and I will know; then I saw their practices.

11:19But I, like a guileless lamb led to be slaughtered, did not know. Against me they devised an evil design, saying: Come, let us put wood into his bread and wipe him out from the land of the living, and his name will certainly be remembered no more.
11:20Lord, who judges justly, who tests kidneys and hearts, may I see the vengeance from Thee upon them, because to Thee I revealed my claim of right.
11:21Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the men of Anathoth who seek my soul, who say: You must certainly not prophesy in the Lord’s name; otherwise you will die by our hands.
11:22Behold, I will visit them; their young men will die by the sword, and their sons and daughters will end their lives in famine,
11:23and no remnant of them will remain, because I will bring evils upon those dwelling in Anathoth in the year of their visitation.

verses.text: 12:1Thou art righteous, Lord, as I make my defense before Thee; nevertheless I will speak judgments with Thee. Why does the impious person’s way prosper? Why did all who commit acts of rejection flourish?
12:2Thou didst plant them, and they took root; they produced children and bore fruit. Thou art near their mouth and far from their kidneys.
12:3And Thou, Lord, knowest me; Thou hast tested my heart before Thee. Purify them for their day of slaughter.
12:4How long will the earth mourn and all the field’s grass dry up because of the evil of those dwelling in it? Livestock and birds vanished, because they said, ‘God will not see our ways.’
12:5Your feet run and exhaust you; how will you prepare yourself against horses? And in a land of peace you have confidence; how will you fare in the Jordan’s raging?
12:6For even your brothers and your father’s house rejected you, and they shouted; they gathered behind you. Do not trust them, because they will speak good things to you.
12:7I have abandoned My house, let go My inheritance, and given My beloved soul into her enemies’ hands.
12:8My inheritance became to Me like a lion in woodland; she raised her voice against Me, therefore I hated her.
12:9Is My inheritance to Me a hyena’s cave, or a cave around her? Go, gather all the field’s wild beasts, and let them come to eat her!
12:10Many shepherds ruined My vineyard, defiled My portion, and made My desirable portion an impassable wilderness.
12:11It was reduced to ruin and destruction; because of Me the whole land utterly vanished, because there is no man who lays it to heart.
12:12Upon every passage through the wilderness those bringing misery came, because the Lord’s sword will devour from one end of the earth to the other; there is no peace for any flesh.
12:13Sow wheat and harvest thorns! Their allotments will not benefit them. Be ashamed of your boasting, of reproach before the Lord.

12:14For thus says the Lord concerning all the evil neighbors who touch My inheritance that I apportioned to My people Israel: Behold, I am tearing them from their land, and I will cast Judah out from their midst.
12:15And after I cast them out, I will return and have mercy on them and settle each in his inheritance and each in his land.
12:16And if they truly learn My people’s way, to swear by My name, ‘The Lord lives,’ as they taught My people to swear by Baal, then they will be built up in the midst of My people.
12:17But if they do not return, I will remove that nation with removal and destruction.

verses.text: 13:1Thus says the Lord: Go, acquire a linen waistcloth for yourself, and put it around your waist, and it will not pass through water.
13:2And I acquired the waistcloth according to the Lord’s word and put it around my waist.
13:3And the Lord’s word came to me, saying:
13:4Take the waistcloth around your waist, and rise and go to the Euphrates, and hide it there in the rock’s opening.
13:5And I went and hid it at the Euphrates, as the Lord commanded me.
13:6And after many days the Lord said to me: Rise, go to the Euphrates, and take from there the waistcloth that I commanded you to hide there.
13:7And I went to the Euphrates River and dug and took the waistcloth from the place where I had buried it. And behold, it was ruined, so that it could certainly be used for nothing.
13:8And the Lord’s word came to me, saying:
13:9Thus says the Lord: Thus I will ruin Judah’s arrogance and Jerusalem’s arrogance,
13:10this great arrogance, those unwilling to obey My words and who went after foreign gods to serve them and bow down to them; and they will be like this waistcloth, which will be used for nothing.

13:11For just as the waistcloth clings around a man’s waist, so I made Israel’s house and all Judah’s house cling to Myself, to become for Me a renowned people, a boast and a glory; and they did not listen to Me.
13:12And you will say to this people: Every wineskin will be filled with wine. And if they say to you, ‘Do we not surely know that every wineskin will be filled with wine?’

13:13then you will say to them: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am filling those dwelling in this land, and their kings, David’s sons who sit on his throne, and the priests and prophets and Judah and all those dwelling in Jerusalem, with intoxication,
13:14and I will scatter them, a man and his brother, their fathers and their sons together. I will not yearn for them, says the Lord, nor spare nor pity them so as to withhold their destruction.
13:15Hear and give ear, and do not exalt yourselves, because the Lord has spoken.
13:16Give glory to the Lord your God before darkness comes and before your feet stumble on dark mountains; you will wait for light, and there is death’s shadow, and they will be placed in darkness.
13:17But if you do not hear, your soul will weep in secret because of arrogance, and your eyes will bring down tears, because the Lord’s flock was crushed.
13:18Say to the king and those exercising power: Humble yourselves and sit down, because your crown of glory was taken down from your head.
13:19The southern cities were shut, and there was no one opening them. Judah was deported; a complete deportation was accomplished.
13:20Lift your eyes, Jerusalem, and see those coming from the north. Where is the flock given to you, the sheep of your glory?
13:21What will you say when they visit you? And you taught them lessons against yourself for rule. Will not labor pains seize you like a woman giving birth?
13:22And if you say in your heart, ‘Why have these things happened to me?’ because of your great injustice your backside was uncovered, so that your heels were put on display.
13:23If an Ethiopian changes his skin and a leopard her markings, then you too will be able to do well, having learned evil things.
13:24And I scattered them like brushwood carried by wind into a wilderness.
13:25This is your lot and portion for your disobeying Me, says the Lord, because you forgot Me and hoped in falsehoods. [1]
13:26And I will uncover your backside over your face, and your dishonor will be seen.

13:27And your adultery and your neighing and the estrangement of your prostitution—on the hills and in the fields I have seen your abominations. Woe to you, Jerusalem, because you were not cleansed after Me! How much longer?

verses.text: 14:1And the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah concerning the lack of rain:
14:2Judea mourned, and her gates were emptied and darkened upon the earth, and Jerusalem’s cry rose.
14:3Her magnates sent their younger ones for water; they came to wells and found no water and brought back their vessels empty.
14:4And the land’s works failed because there was no rain; the farmers were ashamed and covered their heads.
14:5And deer in the field gave birth and abandoned their young, because there was no pasture.
14:6Wild donkeys stood in wooded valleys; they drew in wind, their eyes failed, because there was no grass, because of a people of injustice.
14:7If our sins stood against us, Lord, act for us for Thine own sake, because our sins before Thee are many, because we sinned against Thee.
14:8Israel’s patient expectation, Lord, Thou savest in a time of evils; why didst Thou become like a sojourner upon the earth and like a native turning aside to a lodging?
14:9Wilt Thou be like a sleeping man, or like a man unable to save? Yet Thou art among us, Lord, and Thy name has been called over us; do not forget us.
14:10Thus says the Lord to this people: They loved to move their feet and did not restrain them, and God was not pleased with them; now He will remember their injustices.
14:11And the Lord said to me: Do not pray for good things for this people,

14:12because if they fast, I will not listen to their supplication, and if they bring whole burnt offerings and sacrifices, I will not be pleased with them, because by sword and famine and death I will bring them to an end.
14:13And I said: O Lord, behold, their prophets prophesy and say, ‘You will not see sword, nor will famine be among you, because I will give truth and peace upon the land and in this place.’

14:14And the Lord said to me: The prophets prophesy false things in My name; I did not send them or command them or speak to them, because they prophesy false visions, divinations, omens, and their heart’s choices to you.

14:15Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the prophets prophesying false things in My name, though I did not send them, who say, ‘Sword and famine will not be upon this land’: They will die a diseased death, and the prophets will be consumed by famine.

14:16And the people to whom they prophesy will be thrown into Jerusalem’s thoroughfares because of sword and famine, and there will be no one burying them, and their wives and sons and daughters; and I will pour their evils upon them.
14:17And you will say this word to them: Bring tears down upon your eyes day and night, and let them not cease, because the daughter of My people was utterly crushed, with a very painful wound.
14:18If I go out to the plain, behold, those wounded by the sword; and if I enter the city, behold, the pain of famine! For priest and prophet went to a land they did not know.

14:19Hast Thou utterly rejected Judah, and has Thy soul departed from Zion? Why didst Thou strike us, and there is no healing for us? We waited for peace, and there were no good things; for a time of healing, and behold, turmoil!
14:20We recognized, Lord, our sins and our fathers’ injustices, because we sinned before Thee.
14:21Abate for Thy name’s sake; do not destroy Thy throne of glory. Remember; do not shatter Thy covenant with us.
14:22Is there among the nations’ idols one who brings rain? Can heaven give its fullness? Is it not Thou Thyself? And we will wait for Thee, because Thou madest all these things.

verses.text: 15:1And the Lord said to me: If Moses and Samuel stand before Me, My soul is not toward them. Send this people away, and let them go out.

15:2And if they say to you, ‘Where shall we go out?’ you will say to them: Thus says the Lord: As many as are for death, to death; as many for sword, to sword; as many for famine, to famine; as many for captivity, to captivity.
15:3And I will exact vengeance upon them in four kinds, says the Lord: the sword for slaughter, dogs for tearing apart, the earth’s wild beasts and heaven’s birds for eating and destruction.
15:4And I will hand them over to distresses for all the earth’s kingdoms because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, concerning all he did in Jerusalem.
15:5Who will spare you, Jerusalem? Who will be afraid for you? Or who will turn back for your peace?
15:6You turned away from Me, says the Lord; you will go backward. And I will stretch out My hand and destroy you, and I will no longer let them go.
15:7And I will scatter them in a dispersion; at My people’s gates they were bereaved; they destroyed My people because of their evils.
15:8Their widows multiplied beyond the sea’s sand. I brought misery upon a young man’s mother at noon; suddenly I cast trembling and haste upon her.

15:9She who bore seven was emptied; her soul grew faint. Her sun set while the day was still at its middle; she was ashamed and reproached. Their remnants I will give to the sword before their enemies.

15:10Woe to me, mother! What sort of man did you give birth to—a man litigating and disputing with the whole earth? I benefited no one, nor did anyone benefit me; my strength failed among those cursing me.
15:11May it be, Master, as they are directed—if I did not stand before Thee in the time of their evils and their affliction, for good toward the enemy!
15:12Will iron be recognized? And a bronze enclosure
15:13is your strength. And I will give your treasures as plunder, an exchange for all your sins and in all your borders.
15:14And I will enslave you all around to your enemies in the land you did not know, because a fire has been kindled from My fury; it will burn upon you.
15:15Lord, remember me and visit me and vindicate me against those pursuing me; do not delay. Know how I received reproach concerning Thee
15:16from those rejecting Thy words. Bring them to an end, and Thy word will become to me rejoicing and my heart’s joy, because Thy name has been called over me, Lord Almighty.
15:17I did not sit in their gathering as they played, but I was reverent before Thy hand. I sat alone because I was filled with bitterness.
15:18Why do those grieving me overpower me? My wound is firm; from where will I be healed? It indeed became to me like false water having no faithfulness.

15:19Therefore thus says the Lord: If you return, I will restore you, and you will stand before Me. If you bring out the honored from the unworthy, you will be as My mouth; and they will turn to you, and you will not turn to them.
15:20And I will make you to this people like a fortified bronze wall, and they will fight against you but certainly will not prevail against you, because I am with you to save you
15:21and to rescue you from the hand of evil people, and I will ransom you from the hand of pestilent people.

verses.text: 16:1And you must not take a wife, says the Lord, Israel’s God,
16:2and no son or daughter will be born to you in this place.
16:3For thus says the Lord concerning the sons and daughters born in this place, and their mothers who bore them, and their fathers who begot them in this land:

16:4They will die a diseased death; they will not be mourned or buried. They will be an example upon the earth’s surface, and for the earth’s wild beasts and heaven’s birds; they will fall by the sword and be consumed by famine.
16:5Thus says the Lord: Do not enter their gathering or go to beat yourself in mourning, and do not mourn them, because I have removed My peace from this people.
16:6They certainly will not mourn them or make cuts, and they will not shave themselves,
16:7and bread certainly will not be broken in their mourning for consolation over one dead; they will not give him a cup for consolation over his father and mother.
16:8You must not enter a house of drinking to sit with them to eat and drink.
16:9Because thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Behold, before your eyes and in your days I am stopping from this place the sound of joy and rejoicing, the voice of bridegroom and bride.

16:10And when you announce all these utterances to this people and they say to you, ‘Why did the Lord speak all these evils against us? What is our injustice, and what is our sin that we sinned before the Lord our God?’
16:11you will say to them: Because your fathers abandoned Me, says the Lord, and went after foreign gods and served them and bowed down to them, and abandoned Me and did not keep My law,
16:12and you acted more wickedly than your fathers, and behold, each of you follows what pleases your evil heart, so as not to obey Me,
16:13and I will cast you away from this land into the land neither you nor your fathers knew, and there you will serve other gods who will give you no mercy.
16:14Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say, ‘The Lord lives, who brought Israel’s sons up from Egypt’s land,’
16:15but, ‘The Lord lives, who brought Israel’s house up from the northern land and all the regions where they were driven.’ And I will restore them to their land that I gave their fathers.

16:16Behold, I am sending the many fishermen, says the Lord, and they will fish for them; and after these things I will send the many hunters, and they will hunt them on every mountain and hill and from the rocks’ openings.
16:17Because My eyes are upon all their ways, and their wrongdoings were not hidden before My eyes.

16:18And I will repay double their injustices and sins, for which they profaned My land with the corpses of their abominations and with their lawless acts, by which they offended against My inheritance.
16:19Lord, my strength and help and refuge in a day of evils, nations will come to Thee from the earth’s extremity and say: How our fathers acquired false idols, and there is no benefit in them!
16:20Will a human make gods for himself? And these are not gods.
16:21Therefore behold, at this time I will show them My hand and make My power known to them, and they will know that My name is Lord.

verses.text: 17:5Cursed is the person who places his hope in a human and will rest the flesh of his arm upon him, and whose heart departs from the Lord;
17:6and he will be like a wild tamarisk in the wilderness; he will not see when good things come, and will dwell among salt-plants and in a wilderness, in a salt land that is not inhabited.
17:7And blessed is the person who has trusted in the Lord, and the Lord will be his hope;

17:8and he will be like a tree flourishing beside waters, and will send its roots toward moisture, and will not fear when heat comes. Wooded stems will be upon it; in a rainless year it will not fear or cease bearing fruit.
17:9The heart is deep beyond all things, and so is a human; and who will know him? [1]
17:10I, the Lord, examine hearts and test kidneys, to give each according to his ways and the fruits of his practices.
17:11A partridge called; it gathered what it did not bear. One makes his wealth without judgment; in the middle of his days they will abandon him, and at his last he will be foolish.
17:12An exalted throne of glory is our sanctuary,
17:13Israel’s patient expectation, Lord, let all who abandoned Thee be ashamed; let those who departed be written upon the earth, because they abandoned the Lord, the fountain of life.

verses.text: 18:1The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah, saying:
18:2Rise and go down to the potter’s house, and there you will hear My words.
18:3And I went down to the potter’s house, and behold, he was doing work upon the stones.
18:4And the vessel he was making fell apart in his hands, and again he made it another vessel, as pleased him to make.
18:5And the Lord’s word came to me, saying:
18:6Can I not shape you as this potter does, house of Israel? Behold, you are like the potter’s clay in My hands. [1]
18:7At last I will speak concerning a nation or kingdom, to remove them and destroy,
18:8and if that nation turns from all their evils, I will change My mind concerning the evils I planned to do to them.
18:9And at last I will speak concerning a nation and kingdom, for it to be rebuilt and planted,
18:10and if they do evil things before Me by not hearing My voice, I will change My mind concerning the good things I spoke of doing for them.

18:11And now say to Judah’s men and those dwelling in Jerusalem: Behold, I am shaping evils against you and devising a design against you. Let each turn from his evil way now, and make your practices better.
18:12And they said: We will be resolute, because we will follow our turnings away, and each will do what pleases his evil heart.
18:13Therefore thus says the Lord: Ask now among the nations: Who heard such horrifying things that virgin Israel committed so greatly?
18:14Will breasts fail from a rock, or snow from Lebanon? Will water borne violently by wind turn aside?
18:15Because My people forgot Me, they burned incense in vain; and they will become weak in their ways, the age-old tracks, to step upon paths having no road for travel,
18:16to make their land a ruin and an eternal hissing; all who pass through it will be astonished and shake their head.
18:17Like a scorching wind I will scatter them before their enemies; I will show them their day of destruction.

18:18And they said: Come, let us devise a design against Jeremiah, because law will not perish from a priest, counsel from the discerning, or word from a prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and we will hear all his words.
18:19Listen to me, Lord, and listen to the voice of my claim of right.

18:20Is evil repaid for good things? For they spoke words together against my soul and hid their punishment for me. Remember my standing before Thee to speak good things for them, to turn Thy fury from them.

18:21Therefore give their sons to famine and gather them into the sword’s hands. Let their women become childless and widowed, their men killed by death, and their young men fallen by the sword in war.
18:22Let there be a cry in their houses; Thou wilt bring robbers upon them suddenly, because they attempted a plan for my capture and hid traps against me.

18:23And Thou, Lord, knewest all their counsel against me for death. Do not acquit their injustices or erase their sins from before Thee. Let their weakness be before Thee; act among them in the time of Thy fury.

20:12Lord, testing righteous things, understanding kidneys and hearts: May I see the vengeance from Thee among them, because to Thee I disclosed my defenses.

21:6And I will strike all this city’s inhabitants, the people and the livestock, with a great death, and they will die.

verses.text: 22:1Thus says the Lord: Go and descend to the house of Judah’s king and speak this word there,

22:15Will you reign because you are provoked in Ahaz your father? They will not eat or drink. It was better for you to do judgment and good righteousness.

verses.text: 23:1O shepherds who scatter and destroy the sheep of My pasture!

23:2Therefore thus says the Lord to those shepherding My people: You scattered My sheep and drove them out without visiting them. Behold, I am exacting justice from you according to your evil practices.
23:3And I will receive the remnant of My people from all the land where I drove them out, and establish them in their pasture; they will increase and multiply.
23:4And I will raise shepherds for them who will tend them, and they will no longer fear or be frightened, says the Lord.
23:5Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will raise up a righteous rising for David. A king will reign and understand, doing judgment and righteousness upon the earth. [1]
23:6In his days Judah will be saved and Israel will dwell confidently. This is his name, which the Lord will call him: Josedek.
23:7Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say, As the Lord lives, who brought Israel’s house up from Egypt’s land,
23:8but, As the Lord lives, who gathered all Israel’s offspring from the northern land and all the countries where He drove them out, and restored them to their land.
23:9Among the prophets my heart was shattered; within me all my bones were shaken. I became like a shattered man, like a person gripped by wine, before the Lord and the splendor of His glory.
23:10Because of these things the land mourned and the wilderness pastures dried up. Their course became evil, and their strength was not so.
23:11Because priest and prophet were defiled, and in My house I saw their evils.
23:12Therefore let their way become a slippery place for them in darkness, and they will be tripped and fall in it, because I will bring evils upon them in their year of visitation, says the Lord.
23:13And among Samaria’s prophets I saw lawless acts: they prophesied through Baal and led My people Israel astray.

23:14And among Jerusalem’s prophets I have seen horrifying things: committing adultery, walking in lies, and supporting evil hands so that no one turns from his evil way. They all became like Sodom to Me, and her inhabitants like Gomorrah.
23:15Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will feed them pain and give them bitter water to drink, because from Jerusalem’s prophets defilement went out into all the land.
23:16Thus says the Lord Almighty: Do not listen to the prophets’ words, because they make a vision futile for themselves. They speak from their own heart and not from the Lord’s mouth.

23:17They say to those rejecting the Lord’s word, You will have peace. To all who walk according to their own wishes, to everyone walking in the wandering of his heart, they said, No evils will come upon you.
23:18Because who stood in the Lord’s standing place and saw His word? Who gave ear and heard?
23:19Behold, a shaking comes from the Lord, and anger goes out into a convulsion; swirling, it will come upon the ungodly.
23:20And the Lord’s fury will no longer turn back until He does it and raises it up from His heart’s undertaking. At the end of the days they will understand these things.
23:21I was not sending the prophets, yet they ran; I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.
23:22And if they had stood in My standing presence and listened to My words, they would have turned My people from their evil practices.
23:23I am a God drawing near, says the Lord, and not a God far away.
23:24If a person hides in hidden places, will I not see him? Do I not fill the heaven and the earth? says the Lord.
23:25I heard what the prophets speak, the false things they prophesy in My name, saying, I dreamed a dream.
23:26How long will it be in the heart of the prophets prophesying false things, and in their prophesying the wishes of their own heart?
23:27They plan to forget My law through their dreams, which each told his neighbor, just as their fathers forgot My name through Baal.
23:28Let the prophet in whom there is a dream tell his dream, and the one to whom My word comes tell My word in truth. What has chaff to do with wheat? So are My words, says the Lord.
23:29Are not My words like blazing fire, says the Lord, and like an axe cutting rock?
23:30Therefore behold, I am against the prophets, says the Lord God, who steal My words, each from his neighbor.
23:31Behold, I am against the prophets who cast out prophecies of the tongue and doze their own dozing.

23:32Behold, I am against the prophets who prophesy false dreams, who told them and led My people astray by their lies and wanderings. I did not send or command them, and they will bring this people no benefit at all.
23:33And if this people, a priest, or a prophet asks you, What is the Lord’s burden? say to them, You are the burden, and I will dash you down, says the Lord.
23:34And the prophet, priest, or people who say, The Lord’s burden—I will exact justice from that person and his household.
23:35For this is what you will say, each to his neighbor and his brother: What did the Lord answer? What did the Lord speak?
23:36And do not name the Lord’s burden again, because a person’s own word will be his burden.
23:37And why did the Lord our God speak?
23:38Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you said this word, The Lord’s burden, though I sent to you saying, Do not say The Lord’s burden,
23:39therefore behold, I seize you and dash you down, along with the city I gave to you and your fathers,
23:40and I will put eternal reproach and eternal dishonor upon you, which will not be forgotten.

verses.text: 24:1The Lord showed me two baskets of figs lying before the Lord’s sanctuary, after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had deported Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, the rulers, craftsmen, prisoners, and rich people from Jerusalem and brought them to Babylon.

verses.text: 26:2For Egypt, concerning the force of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, who was beside the Euphrates River at Carchemish and whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim king of Judah:

26:25I am taking vengeance for Amon her son upon Pharaoh and those who trust him.

26:27But do not fear, My slave Jacob, nor be terrified, Israel, for I am saving you from afar and your offspring from their captivity. Jacob will return, be quiet, and sleep, and no one will trouble him.

26:28Do not fear, My servant Jacob, says the Lord, for I am with you. I will make an end of every nation where I thrust you out, but I certainly will not make you perish. I will discipline you for judgment and certainly will not acquit you.

verses.text: 27:1The Lord’s word that He spoke against Babylon:
27:2Announce among the nations and make it heard; do not hide it. Say, Babylon has been captured! Bel was disgraced, the fearless one; the delicate one was handed over, Marodach.
27:3A nation came up against her from the north; it will make her land a ruin, with no one living in it, from human to livestock.
27:4In those days and at that time, Israel’s sons and Judah’s sons will come together; walking and weeping, they will go seeking the Lord their God.
27:5They will ask the way as far as Zion, for they will turn their faces here. They will come and take refuge with the Lord God, for an everlasting covenant will not be forgotten.
27:6My people became lost sheep; their shepherds thrust them away and led them astray upon the mountains. They went from mountain to hill and forgot their resting place.
27:7All who found them consumed them. Their enemies said, Let us not release them, because they sinned against the Lord, the pasture of righteousness, who gathered their fathers.
27:8Separate yourselves from Babylon’s midst and the Chaldeans’ land; come out and become like dragons before sheep.
27:9I am rousing assemblies of nations against Babylon from the north. They will deploy against her; from there she will be captured. Like a discerning warrior’s missile, it will not return empty.
27:10Chaldea will become plunder; all who plunder her will be filled.
27:11because you rejoiced and boasted while plundering My inheritance, because you leaped like little cattle in pasture and butted like bulls,
27:12your mother was deeply ashamed—a mother for good things, last of nations, a wilderness.
27:13Because of the Lord’s anger she will not be inhabited and will entirely disappear. Everyone passing through Babylon will look gloomy, and they will hiss at every wound of hers.
27:14Deploy against Babylon all around, all who stretch the bow. Shoot at her; do not spare your arrows.
27:15Clap against her! Her hands were disabled, her battlements fell, and her wall was demolished. For this is vengeance from God; take vengeance upon her. Do to her as she did.
27:16Destroy seed from Babylon, the one holding a sickle at harvest. Before the Greek sword, each will return to his people and flee to his land.
27:17Israel is a wandering sheep driven away by lions. First Assyria’s king ate him; later this one, Babylon’s king, ate his bones.
27:18Therefore thus says the Lord: I am taking vengeance upon Babylon’s king and his land, as I took vengeance upon Assyria’s king.
27:19I will restore Israel to his pasture. He will graze on Carmel, on Ephraim’s mountain, and in Gilead, and his soul will be filled.

27:20In those days and at that time they will seek Israel’s injustice, and it will not exist, and Judah’s sins, and they certainly will not be found, for I will be merciful to those left upon the land, says the Lord.
27:21Go fiercely against her and her inhabitants. Take vengeance, sword, and make her disappear, says the Lord; do everything I command you.
27:22A sound of war and great shattering in the Chaldeans’ land!
27:23How the hammer of the whole earth was snapped and shattered! How Babylon became a ruin among nations!
27:24They will attack you and you will be captured, Babylon, without knowing it. You were found and taken because you resisted the Lord.
27:25The Lord opened His treasury and brought out the instruments of His anger, for the Lord God has work in the Chaldeans’ land,
27:26for her times have arrived. Open her storehouses; search her like a cave and destroy her. Let no remnant of her remain.
27:27Dry up all her fruits, and let them go down to slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their vengeance.
27:28A sound of those fleeing and being rescued from Babylon’s land, announcing in Zion vengeance from the Lord our God!

27:29Give orders against Babylon to many, to everyone drawing a bow. Encamp against her all around; let none of her people escape. Repay her according to her works; do to her all she did, for she resisted the Lord, Israel’s holy God.
27:30Therefore her young men will fall in her squares, and all her warriors will be thrown down, said the Lord.
27:31I am against you, insolent woman, says the Lord, for your day has come, the time of your vengeance.
27:32Your insolence will grow weak and fall, with no one to raise it. I will kindle fire in her forest, and it will devour everything around her.
27:33Thus says the Lord: Israel’s sons and Judah’s sons have been oppressed together. All who captured them oppressed them, because they did not want to release them.
27:34The One redeeming them is strong; the Lord Almighty is His name. He will judge a case against His adversaries, to remove the land, and He will provoke Babylon’s inhabitants.
27:35A sword against the Chaldeans, Babylon’s inhabitants, her nobles, and her discerning men!
27:36A sword against her warriors, and they will be disabled!

27:37A sword against their horses and chariots! A sword against their warriors and the mixed people within her, and they will become like women! A sword against her treasures, and they will be scattered!
27:38She trusted in her water, and they will be ashamed, for it is a land of carved images, and in the islands where they boasted.
27:39Therefore apparitions will live on the islands, and daughters of sirens will live in her. She certainly will never again be inhabited.
27:40As God overturned Sodom, Gomorrah, and their bordering places, said the Lord, no person will live there, and no human being will reside there.
27:41A people is coming from the north; a great nation and many kings will be roused from the earth’s farthest part,
27:42holding bow and dagger. It is insolent and certainly will not show mercy. Their voice will sound like the sea. They will ride horses, prepared like fire for war against you, daughter Babylon.
27:43Babylon’s king heard the report about them, and his hands were disabled. Distress seized him, birth pains like a woman giving birth.

27:44Like a lion he will come up from the Jordan into Aitham’s place, for I will quickly drive them away from her and appoint every young man over her. For who is like Me? Who will resist Me, and what shepherd can stand before Me?

27:45Therefore hear the Lord’s counsel that He has planned against Babylon and His purposes against the resident Chaldeans: Surely the lambs of their sheep will be destroyed; surely pasture will disappear from them.
27:46For at the sound of Babylon’s capture the earth will shake, and a cry will be heard among the nations.
