verses.text: 28:1Thus says the Lord: I am rousing a destroying hot wind against Babylon and against the Chaldeans who live there.
28:2I will send insolent men to Babylon; they will abuse her and ravage her land. Woe upon Babylon all around on the day of her affliction!
28:3Against her let the archer stretch his bow, and let the man who has armor put it on. Do not spare her young men; obliterate her whole force.
28:4Wounded men will fall in the Chaldeans’ land, and pierced men outside her.
28:5For Israel and Judah have not been widowed of their God, of the Lord Almighty, because their land was filled with injustice from Israel’s holy ones.
28:6Flee from Babylon’s midst; each of you save your life. Do not be cast away in her injustice, for her time of vengeance is from the Lord; He is repaying her recompense.
28:7Babylon was a golden cup in the Lord’s hand, making the whole earth drunk. Nations drank her wine; therefore they were shaken.
28:8Suddenly Babylon fell and was shattered. Lament her! Take resin for her corruption, if somehow she may be healed.
28:9We treated Babylon, but she was not healed. Let us leave her; let each of us go to our own land, for her judgment reached heaven and rose to the stars.
28:10The Lord has brought forth His judgment. Come, let us announce in Zion the works of the Lord our God.
28:11Prepare the arrows; fill the quivers. The Lord roused the spirit of the Medes’ king, for His anger against Babylon is to destroy her. This is the Lord’s vengeance, vengeance for His people.
28:12Raise a signal on Babylon’s walls; set up quivers, raise guards, prepare weapons, for the Lord has undertaken and will do what He spoke against Babylon’s inhabitants,
28:13who dwell beside many waters and her abundance of treasures. Your end has truly come to your inward parts.
28:14For the Lord swore by His arm: I will fill you with people like locusts, and those coming down will speak out against you.
28:15He makes the earth by His strength, prepares the inhabited world by His wisdom, and stretched out heaven by His understanding.
28:16At His voice He set a sound of water in heaven and brought clouds up from the earth’s end. He made lightning for rain and brought light out of His treasuries.
28:17Every person became foolish, without knowledge; every goldsmith was disgraced by his carvings, because they cast false things, and there is no spirit in them.
28:18They are vain, mocked works; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
28:19Jacob’s portion is not like this, for the One who formed all things is Himself his inheritance. The Lord is His name.
28:20You scatter instruments of war for Me. In you I will scatter nations, and from you I will remove kings.
28:21In you I will scatter horse and rider; in you I will scatter chariots and their riders.
28:22In you I will scatter young man and virgin; in you I will scatter man and woman.
28:23In you I will scatter shepherd and flock; in you I will scatter farmer and farmland; in you I will scatter your leaders and generals.
28:24I will repay Babylon and all the Chaldeans who live there for all the evils they did against Zion before your eyes, says the Lord.
28:25I am against you, ruined mountain that ruins the whole earth. I will stretch My hand against you, roll you down from the rocks, and make you like a burned mountain.
28:26They will certainly not take from you a cornerstone or a foundation stone, for you will be a ruin for ever, says the Lord.

28:27Raise a signal on the earth; sound a trumpet among the nations. Consecrate nations against her; give orders against her to Ararat’s kingdoms from Me and to the Ashkenazites. Set up arrow batteries against her; bring up horses against her like a multitude of locusts.
28:28Consecrate nations against her: the king of the Medes and of all the earth, his leaders and all his generals.
28:29The earth was shaken and suffered, for the Lord’s purpose rose against Babylon, to make Babylon’s land a ruin, no longer inhabited.
28:30Babylon’s warrior has ceased fighting; they will sit there in confinement. Their power was crushed; they became like women. Her dwellings were burned; her bars were shattered.
28:31Pursuer will pursue to meet pursuer, and announcer to meet announcer, to tell Babylon’s king that his city has been captured;
28:32from the extremity of his crossings they were taken, and their gatherings were burned with fire, and his warriors are going out.
28:33For thus says the Lord: The houses of Babylon’s king will be threshed like a threshing floor ready for use; a little longer, and her harvest will come.
28:34Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon devoured me, divided me, seized me, a thin vessel. He swallowed me like a dragon, filled his belly, and drove me from my luxury.
28:35My toils and miseries be upon Babylon, the woman dwelling in Zion will say; my blood be upon the Chaldeans who live there, Jerusalem will say.
28:36Therefore thus says the Lord: I will judge your adversary and avenge you; I will lay her sea waste and dry her spring.
28:37Babylon will become a ruin and will not be inhabited.
28:38Together they were roused like lions and like lions’ cubs.
28:39In their heat I will give them a drink and make them drunk, so that they are stupefied and sleep an everlasting sleep and certainly do not rise, says the Lord.
28:40I will bring them down like lambs to slaughter and like rams with young goats.
28:41How the boast of the whole earth was captured and hunted! How Babylon became a ruin among the nations!
28:42The sea rose over Babylon with the sound of its waves, and she was covered.
28:43Her cities became a waterless and untrodden land; not one person will live there, nor will any human lodge there.
28:44I will exact vengeance on Babylon and bring what she swallowed out of her mouth. Nations will certainly no longer gather to her.
28:49And in Babylon wounded men from all the earth will fall.
28:50You who escape from the land, go on; do not stand still. You who are far away, remember the Lord, and let Jerusalem rise in your hearts.
28:51We were disgraced, for we heard our reproach; dishonor covered our face. Foreigners entered our holy places, the Lord’s house.
28:52Therefore days are coming, says the Lord, when I will exact vengeance on her carvings, and wounded men will fall throughout her land.
28:53Even if Babylon rises as high as heaven and fortifies the height of her strength, those who destroy her will come from Me, says the Lord.
28:54A sound of crying in Babylon, a great shattering in the Chaldeans’ land!
28:55For the Lord destroyed Babylon and silenced her loud voice sounding like many waters; He gave her voice over to destruction.
28:56For misery came upon Babylon. Her warriors were captured; their bow is terrified, because God repays them; the Lord repays her recompense.
28:57He will make her leaders and wise men and generals thoroughly drunk, says the King, whose name is the Lord Almighty.
28:58Thus says the Lord: Babylon’s wall was broadened; it will be utterly demolished, and her high gates burned. Peoples will not labor in vain, and nations will perish at the beginning.

28:59The word the Lord commanded Jeremiah the prophet to tell Seraiah son of Neriah son of Maaseiah when he went from Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was an official over gifts.
28:60Jeremiah wrote in one scroll all the evils that would come upon Babylon, all these words written against Babylon.
28:61Jeremiah said to Seraiah: When you arrive in Babylon, you will see and read all these words,
28:62and say, Lord, Lord, Thou spakest against this place to destroy it and leave no inhabitants in it, from human to livestock, for it will be a ruin for ever.
28:63When you finish reading this scroll, bind a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates,
28:64and say, Thus Babylon will sink and certainly not rise because of the evils I am bringing upon her.

verses.text: 29:1Concerning the people of another tribe.

29:2Thus says the Lord: Waters are rising from the north and will become a flooding torrent. It will flood the land and its fullness, the city and those living in it. People will cry out, and all the land’s inhabitants will shout aloud.
29:3At the sound of his onrush, of the hooves of his feet, the shaking of his chariots, and the noise of his wheels, fathers did not turn back to their sons, because their hands failed,
29:4on the day coming to destroy all the people of another tribe. I will obliterate Tyre and Sidon and all the remainder of their assistance, for the Lord will destroy the survivors of the islands.
29:5Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon and the survivors of the Anakim have been cast away. How long will you strike,
29:6sword of the Lord? How long will you not be quiet? Return to your sheath; rest and be lifted away!
29:7How will it be quiet? The Lord commanded it to rise against Ashkelon, against the coastal places, against those remaining.

verses.text: 30:1For Idumea, thus says the Lord: There is no longer wisdom in Teman; counsel perished from the discerning; their wisdom went away.
30:2Their place was deceived. Go deep to dwell, inhabitants of Dedan, for he did difficult things; I brought them upon him at the time I visited him.
30:3For grape gatherers came to you; they will leave you no remnants. Like thieves by night they will lay their hand upon you.
30:4For I dragged Esau away and uncovered their secrets; they certainly cannot hide. They perished by the hand of his brother and his neighbor, and it is not possible
30:5for your orphan to remain so that he may live. And I will live, and widows have trusted in Me.
30:6For thus said the Lord: Those for whom there was no law to drink the cup drank it. And you, though acquitted, certainly will not be acquitted, for you will certainly drink.
30:7For I swore by Myself, says the Lord, that you will become an untrodden place, a reproach, and a curse in her midst, and all her cities will be deserted for ever.
30:8I heard a report from the Lord, and He sent messengers to the nations: Gather and come against her; rise for war!
30:9I made you small among nations, easily despised among people.
30:10Your playfulness assailed you; your heart’s insolence destroyed holes in rocks and seized the strength of a high hill. For he raised his nest like an eagle; from there I will bring you down.
30:11Idumea will become an untrodden place; everyone passing by her will hiss.
30:12As Sodom, Gomorrah, and her neighboring places were overturned, said the Lord Almighty, no person will settle there, and no human being will live there.

30:13Like a lion he will come up from Jordan’s midst into Aitham’s place, for I will quickly drive them away from her. Appoint the young men over her. For who is like Me? Who will resist Me, and what shepherd can stand before Me?

30:14Therefore hear the Lord’s counsel that He planned against Idumea and His purpose against Teman’s inhabitants: Surely the smallest sheep will be swept together; surely their dwelling will be made untrodden over her.
30:15For at the sound of their fall the earth shook, and your cry was heard at the sea.
30:16Like an eagle he will look and stretch his wings over her fortifications. That day Idumea’s strong men’s hearts will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
30:17For Ammon’s sons, thus said the Lord: Are there no sons in Israel, or have they no one to inherit? Why did Melchom take Gad, and will their people live in their cities?

30:18Therefore days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make the din of wars heard against Rabbath. They will become an untrodden place and a destruction, her altars will be burned with fire, and Israel will receive his rule.

30:19Shout aloud, Heshbon, for Gai perished! Cry out, daughters of Rabbath; put on sackcloth, be seized with distress, and beat yourselves over Melchom, for he will go into deportation, his priests and rulers together.
30:20Why do you exult in the plains of the Anakim, daughter of dishonor, trusting in her treasures and saying, Who will come against me?
30:21I am bringing fear upon you, said the Lord, from all your surroundings. You will be scattered, each straight ahead, and there will be no one gathering.
30:23For Kedar, queen of the courtyard, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck. Thus said the Lord: Rise and go up against Kedar, and fill the sons of Kedem!
30:24They will take their tents and sheep, their garments, all their equipment, and camels for themselves. Call destruction against them on every side!
30:25Flee far away; go deep to dwell, you who stay in the courtyard, for Babylon’s king planned counsel against you and devised a purpose against you.
30:26Rise and go up against a stable nation living in refreshment, with neither doors nor pins nor bars; they lodge alone.

30:27Their camels will become plunder and their numerous livestock destruction. I will winnow them to every wind, those shorn before their faces; from every side of them I will bring their rout, said the Lord.
30:28The courtyard will become an abode for ostriches, untrodden for ever. No person will settle there; no human being will live there.
30:29For Damascus: Hamath and Arpad were ashamed because they heard an evil report. They were distraught and angry; they certainly cannot rest.
30:30Damascus grew feeble and turned to flight; trembling seized her.
30:31How did he not abandon My city? They loved a village.
30:32Therefore young men will fall in your squares, and all your warriors will fall, says the Lord.
30:33I will kindle fire in Damascus’s wall, and it will devour the quarters of Ader’s son.

verses.text: 31:1For Moab, thus said the Lord: Woe to Nebo, for she perished! Kiriathaim was taken; Amath was disgraced and defeated.
31:2There is no longer healing for Moab, a boast in Heshbon. They devised evils against her: We cut her off from a nation, and she will certainly cease. A sword will walk behind you.
31:3For a sound of people crying out comes from Horonaim: destruction and great shattering!
31:4Moab was shattered; announce it in Zogora.
31:5For Alaoth was filled with weeping; he will go up weeping on Horonaim’s road. You heard a cry of shattering:
31:6Flee and save your lives, and you will be like a wild donkey in the wilderness!
31:7Because you trusted in your fortifications, you too will be seized. Chemosh will go into deportation, his priests and rulers together.
31:8Destruction will come upon every city; no city will be saved. The valley will perish and the plain be destroyed, as the Lord said.
31:9Give signs to Moab, for she will surely be kindled; all her cities will become an untrodden place. From where will an inhabitant come to her?
31:10Accursed is one who does the Lord’s works carelessly, removing his sword from blood.
31:11Moab rested from childhood and trusted in his glory. He did not pour from vessel to vessel or go into deportation. Therefore his taste remained in him and his scent did not fade.
31:12Therefore days are coming, says the Lord, when I will send him tilters who will tip him, thin out his vessels, and cut up his horns.
31:13Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as Israel’s house was ashamed of Bethel, their hope, having trusted in them.
31:14How will you say, We are strong, and a man strong for warfare?
31:15Moab perished, his city, and his choice young men went down to slaughter.
31:16Moab’s day is near to coming, and his calamity is very swift.
31:17Move in lament for him, all who surround him, all who know his name. Say, How the renowned staff is shattered, the rod of grandeur!
31:18Come down from glory and sit in dampness, resident Dibon. Be crushed, for Moab perished; he came up against you, ruining your fortification.
31:19Stand on the road and look, you who live in Aroer. Ask the one fleeing and the one being saved, and say, What happened?
31:20Moab was ashamed, for he was shattered. Wail and cry out; announce at Arnon that Moab perished.
31:21Judgment is coming into the land of Misor: upon Chailon, Jahzah, and Mophath,
31:22upon Dibon, Nebo, and the house of Deblathaim,
31:23upon Kiriathaim, the house of Gamol, and the house of Maon,
31:24upon Kerioth, Bosor, and all Moab’s cities, far and near.
31:25Moab’s horn was broken and his effort shattered.
31:26Make him drunk, for he magnified himself against the Lord. Moab will strike with his hand and become a laughingstock himself.
31:27Was not Israel a laughingstock to you? Was he found in your thefts, that you made war on him?
31:28Moab’s inhabitants left the cities and lived among rocks. They became like doves nesting among rocks at a pit’s mouth.
31:29I heard Moab’s insolence; he acted very insolently—his insolence and arrogance—and his heart was lifted up.
31:30But I knew his works. Not his sufficiency; he did not act so.
31:31Therefore wail over Moab from every side; cry out over the men of Kiradas of drought.
31:32Like the weeping for Jazer, I will weep for you, vine of Sibmah. Your branches crossed the sea and reached Jazer. Destruction fell upon your summer fruit and your grape gatherers.
31:33Joy and gladness were boiled away from Moab’s land, and wine was upon your winepresses. They did not tread in the morning or in the evening; they did not make an aidad shout.
31:34From Heshbon’s cry as far as Elealeh, their cities raised their voice; from Zogor to Horonaim and Aglath-salisia, for even Nebrim’s water will become a burning.
31:35I will destroy Moab, says the Lord, as he goes up to an altar and burns incense to his gods.
31:36Therefore my heart, Moab, will hum like flutes; my heart will hum like a flute for Kiradas’s people. Therefore what he acquired perished from a person.
31:37They will shave every head in every place; every beard will be shaved, all hands will beat themselves, and on every waist is sackcloth.
31:38And on all Moab’s rooftops and in her squares—for I shattered Moab, says the Lord, like a vessel for which there is no use.
31:39How he has changed! How Moab turned his back! He was ashamed, and Moab became a laughingstock and an object of resentment to all around her.
31:40For thus said the Lord:
31:41Akkarioth was taken and the fortifications seized.
31:42Moab will perish from being a multitude, for he magnified himself against the Lord.
31:43Trap, fear, and pit are upon you, resident Moab.
31:44One who flees from fear will fall into the pit, and one who climbs from the pit will be caught in the trap, for I will bring these things upon Moab in the year of her visitation.

verses.text: 32:15Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Take this cup of unmixed wine from My hand, and give it to all the nations to whom I send you to drink,
32:16and they will drink, vomit, and go mad before the sword I am sending among them.
32:17And I took the cup from the Lord’s hand and gave it to the nations to whom the Lord sent me to drink:
32:18Jerusalem, Judah’s cities, Judah’s kings, and its rulers, to make them a desolation, an untrodden place, and a hissing;
32:19and Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his nobles, and all his people;
32:20and all his mixed population, all the Philistine kings, Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and Ashdod’s remnant;
32:21and Idumea, the Moabite land, and Ammon’s sons;
32:22and all Tyre’s kings, Sidon’s kings, and the kings across the sea;
32:23and Dedan, Teman, Ros, and everyone shorn about his face;
32:24and all the mixed populations lodging in the wilderness;
32:25and all Elam’s kings and all the Persian kings;
32:26and all the kings from the east, far and near, each with his brother, and all the kingdoms upon the face of the earth.
32:27And say to them: Thus said the Lord Almighty: Drink, get drunk, and vomit; you will fall and certainly not rise before the sword I am sending among you.
32:28And when they are unwilling to receive the cup from your hand to drink, say: Thus said the Lord: You will certainly drink.
32:29Because I am beginning to bring harm in the city upon which My name was named, and you will certainly not be cleansed, because I am summoning a sword against those dwelling upon the earth.

32:30And prophesy these words against them and say: The Lord will give an oracle from on high; from His holy place He will raise His voice. He will give an oracular word over His place, and they will answer with Aidad, like grape-gatherers. And upon those dwelling upon the earth,
32:31destruction comes upon a part of the earth, because the Lord has a judgment among the nations. He enters judgment with all flesh, and the ungodly were given to the sword, says the Lord.
32:32Thus said the Lord: Behold, evils come from nation to nation, and a great whirlwind goes out from the earth’s farthest end.
32:33And those wounded by the Lord on the Lord’s day will lie from one part of the earth to another. They will certainly not be buried; they will be dung upon the earth’s face.
32:34Raise a shout, shepherds, and cry out; beat yourselves in mourning, rams of the sheep, because your days for slaughter have been fulfilled, and you will fall like choice rams.
32:35And flight will perish from the shepherds, and salvation from the rams of the sheep.
32:36A sound of shepherds crying and of sheep and rams shouting, because the Lord destroyed their grazing places,
32:37and the remnants of peace will cease before the anger of My fury.
32:38Like a lion He abandoned His lodging, because their land became an untrodden place before the great sword.

verses.text: 33:1At the beginning of the reign of King Jehoiakim son of Josiah, this word came from the Lord:

33:2Thus said the Lord: Stand in the courtyard of the Lord’s house and deliver an oracle to all the Judeans and all who come to bow down in the Lord’s house—all the words I commanded you to deliver to them. Do not take away a word.
33:3Perhaps they will hear and turn, each from his evil way, and I will cease from the evils I plan to do to them because of their evil practices.
33:4And say: Thus said the Lord: If you do not hear Me, walking in My ordinances that I set before your face,
33:5listening to the words of My servants the prophets whom I send to you from early morning, and have sent—though you did not listen to Me—
33:6then I will make this house like Shiloh and make the city a curse to all the nations of all the earth.
33:7And the priests, false prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the Lord’s house.
33:8And when Jeremiah stopped speaking everything the Lord commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests, false prophets, and all the people seized him, saying: You must die!
33:9Because you prophesied in the Lord’s name, saying, This house will be like Shiloh and this city will be emptied of inhabitants. And all the people assembled against Jeremiah in the Lord’s house.

39:9I acquired the field of Hanamel, my father’s brother’s son, and weighed out to him seventeen shekels of silver.

verses.text: 42:1The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim king of Judah:
42:2Go to the house of the Rechabites. Bring them into the Lord’s house, into one of the courts, and give them wine to drink.
42:3I brought out Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah son of Habazziniah, his brothers, his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites.

42:4I brought them into the Lord’s house, into the chamber of the sons of Hananiah son of Gedaliah, the man of God. It is near the house of the rulers above the house of Maaseiah son of Shallum, who guards the court.
42:5I set before them an earthenware jar of wine and cups, and said, Drink wine.
42:6They said, We certainly will not drink wine, because Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, commanded us: Neither you nor your sons must ever drink wine.
42:7You must not build a house or sow seed, and you must not have a vineyard. You must live in tents all your days, so that you may live many days on the land where you spend your time.
42:8We have obeyed the voice of Jonadab our father by not drinking wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters,
42:9and by not building houses to live there. We have had no vineyard, field, or sown crop.
42:10We lived in tents, obeying and doing everything Jonadab our father commanded us.
42:11When Nebuchadnezzar invaded the land, we said, Come in, let us enter Jerusalem to escape the Chaldean force and the Assyrian force. So we were living there.
42:12The Lord’s word came to me:
42:13Thus says the Lord: Go and say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem’s inhabitants, Will you really not accept discipline and hear My words?

42:14The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab upheld the word he commanded his children, not to drink wine, and they drank none. Yet I spoke to you from early morning and kept speaking, and you did not listen.

42:15I sent you My servants the prophets, saying, Each of you, turn from his evil way and improve your practices. Do not follow other gods to serve them, and you will live on the land I gave you and your fathers. But you did not incline your ears or listen.
42:16The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab upheld their father’s command, but this people did not obey Me.
42:17Therefore thus said the Lord: I am bringing upon Judah and Jerusalem’s inhabitants all the calamities I pronounced against them.
42:18Therefore thus said the Lord: Because the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab obeyed their father’s command, doing as their father commanded them,
42:19there will certainly never fail a man from the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab standing before Me all the earth’s days.

verses.text: 43:1In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, the Lord’s word came to me:

43:2Take a writing roll and write on it all the words I have delivered to you as oracles concerning Jerusalem, Judah, and all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah king of Judah until today.
43:3Perhaps Judah’s house will hear all the calamities I intend to bring upon them, so that they turn from their evil way and I may be merciful toward their injustices and sins.
43:4Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and he wrote on a writing roll, from Jeremiah’s mouth, all the Lord’s words which He had delivered to him as oracles.
43:5Jeremiah instructed Baruch, I am under guard and cannot enter the Lord’s house.
43:6Read from this roll in the people’s hearing at the Lord’s house on a fast day, and read it to all Judah’s people coming from their city.
43:7Perhaps their appeal for mercy will fall before the Lord, and they will turn from their evil way, for great are the Lord’s wrath and anger which He has pronounced against this people.
43:8Baruch did everything Jeremiah instructed him, reading the Lord’s words from the document in the Lord’s house.
43:9In King Jehoiakim’s eighth year, in the ninth month, all the people in Jerusalem and Judah’s house assembled for a fast before the Lord.

43:10Baruch read Jeremiah’s words from the document in the Lord’s house, in the house of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court at the entrance of the New Gate of the Lord’s house, in all the people’s hearing.
43:11Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the Lord’s words from the document.

43:12He went down to the king’s house, to the scribe’s house. All the rulers were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shelemiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the rulers.
43:13Micaiah reported to them all the words he had heard when Baruch read in the people’s hearing.

43:14All the rulers sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi to Baruch son of Neriah, saying, Take in your hand the roll from which you are reading to the people, and come. Baruch took the roll and went down to them.
43:15They said to him, Read it again to us. Baruch read it.
43:16When they heard all the words, they consulted one another and said, Let us certainly report all these words to the king.
43:17They asked Baruch, Where did all these words you wrote come from?
43:18Baruch said, Jeremiah reported all these words to me from his mouth, and I wrote them in a document.
43:19They said to Baruch, Go and hide, you and Jeremiah. Let no one know where you are.
43:20They entered the court to see the king, leaving the roll for safekeeping in Elishama’s house, and reported all the words to the king.
43:21The king sent Jehudi to fetch the roll. He took it from Elishama’s house, and Jehudi read it to the king and all the rulers standing around him.
43:22The king was sitting in a winter house, with a fire brazier before him.
43:23When Jehudi read three or four columns, the king cut them off with the scribe’s knife and threw them into the fire on the brazier, until the whole roll was consumed in the brazier’s fire.
43:24Neither the king nor his servants who heard all these words sought anything or tore their garments.
43:25Elnathan, Gedaliah, and Gemariah advised the king not to burn the roll.
43:26The king ordered Jerahmeel the king’s son and Seraiah son of Azriel to arrest Baruch and Jeremiah. But they were hidden.
43:27After the king burned the roll—all the words Baruch had written from Jeremiah’s mouth—the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah:
43:28Take another roll again and write all the words that were on the roll which King Jehoiakim burned.
43:29Say, Thus said the Lord: You burned this roll, saying, Why did you write in it that Babylon’s king will certainly enter and destroy this land, and people and animals will cease from it?
43:30Therefore thus said the Lord concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one sitting on David’s throne. His carcass will be thrown out in the day’s heat and the night’s frost.
43:31I will visit him, his family, and his servants, and bring upon them, Jerusalem’s inhabitants, and Judah’s land all the calamities I pronounced to them, but they did not listen.
43:32Baruch took another roll and wrote on it, from Jeremiah’s mouth, all the words of the document Jehoiakim burned. Still more words like these were added to it.

verses.text: 44:1Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned in place of Jehoiakim; Nebuchadnezzar had made him king over Judah.
44:2Neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land obeyed the Lord’s words, which He spoke through Jeremiah.
44:3King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah, saying, Please pray for us to the Lord.
44:4Jeremiah came and passed through the midst of the city; they had not put him in prison.
44:5Pharaoh’s force came out of Egypt. The Chaldeans heard the report about them and withdrew from Jerusalem.
44:6The Lord’s word came to Jeremiah:
44:7Thus said the Lord: Tell Judah’s king, who sent to you to seek Me, Pharaoh’s force, which came out to help you, will return to Egypt’s land.
44:8The Chaldeans themselves will return, fight this city, seize it, and burn it with fire.
44:9For thus said the Lord: Do not suppose within yourselves, The Chaldeans will flee and leave us. They certainly will not leave.
44:10Even if you struck the whole Chaldean force fighting you and some were left pierced through, each in his place, these would rise and burn this city with fire.
44:11When the Chaldean force withdrew from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh’s force,
44:12Jeremiah left Jerusalem to go to Benjamin’s land, to buy from there among the people.
44:13At Benjamin’s Gate there was a man with whom he lodged, Sarouiah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah. He arrested Jeremiah, saying, You are fleeing to the Chaldeans!
44:14He said, A lie! I am not fleeing to the Chaldeans. But Sarouiah would not listen to him; he arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the rulers.
44:15The rulers were embittered against Jeremiah. They struck him and sent him into the house of Jonathan the scribe, which they had made into a prison house.
44:16Jeremiah entered the pit-house and the chereth and stayed there many days.
44:17Zedekiah sent and summoned him. The king secretly asked him whether there was a word from the Lord. He said, There is. You will be handed over to Babylon’s king.
44:18Jeremiah said to the king, How have I wronged you, your servants, or this people, that you are putting me in prison?
44:19Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, Babylon’s king certainly will not come against this land?
44:20Now, lord king, let my appeal for mercy fall before you. Why send me back to Jonathan the scribe’s house—and will I not die there?
44:21The king gave orders, and they put him into the prison house, giving him one loaf a day from outside where they bake, until the city’s loaves ran out. Jeremiah remained in the prison court.

verses.text: 45:1Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, and Jehucal son of Shelemiah heard the words Jeremiah was speaking to the people:
45:2Thus said the Lord: Whoever remains in this city will die by sword and famine. Whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live; his life will be his gain, and he will live.
45:3For thus said the Lord: This city will certainly be handed over to the force of Babylon’s king, and he will seize it.

45:4They said to the king, Let that man be killed! By speaking these words to them he weakens the hands of the fighters left in the city and of all the people. This man delivers oracles of evil to this people, not peace.
45:5The king said, He is in your hands—for the king was unable to oppose them.
45:6They threw him into the pit of Malchiah the king’s son in the prison court and lowered him into the pit. There was no water in it, only mire, and he was in the mire.
45:7Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, who was in the king’s house, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the pit. The king was at Benjamin’s Gate.
45:8He went out to him, spoke to the king, and said:
45:9You have acted wickedly in what you did, killing this man through hunger, for there are no more loaves in the city.
45:10The king instructed Ebed-melech, Take thirty men from here under your command and bring him up from the pit so that he does not die.
45:11Ebed-melech took the men and entered the king’s underground house. He took old rags and old ropes from there and threw them down to Jeremiah in the pit.
45:12He said, Put these beneath the ropes. Jeremiah did so.
45:13They pulled him with the ropes and brought him up from the pit. Jeremiah remained in the prison court.
45:14The king sent and summoned him to himself, to the aselisi house in the Lord’s house. The king said to him, I will ask you something. Please hide no word from me.
45:15Jeremiah said to the king, If I tell you, will you not certainly put me to death? And if I advise you, you certainly will not listen to me.
45:16The king swore to him, As the Lord lives, who made this life for us, I will not kill you or hand you over to these men.

45:17Jeremiah said to him, Thus said the Lord: If you go out to Babylon’s king’s commanders, your life will be spared and this city will certainly not be burned with fire. You and your household will live.
45:18But if you do not go out, this city will be handed over to the Chaldeans and they will burn it with fire. You certainly will not be saved.
45:19The king said to Jeremiah, I am concerned about the Judeans who have fled to the Chaldeans, lest they hand me over to them and mock me.
45:20Jeremiah said, They certainly will not hand you over. Hear the Lord’s word which I speak to you, and it will be better for you; your life will be spared.
45:21But if you are unwilling to go out, this is the word the Lord showed me:

45:22All the women left in Judah’s king’s house were being brought out to Babylon’s king’s rulers. They said, Your peaceful friends deceived you and will overpower you. They will bring your feet to rest in slippery places; they turned away from you.
45:23They will bring your wives and children out to the Chaldeans. You certainly will not be saved, for Babylon’s king will seize you, and this city will be burned.
45:24The king said to him, Let no one learn anything of these words, and you certainly will not die.
45:25If the rulers hear that I spoke to you, come to you, and say, Tell us what the king said to you. Hide nothing from us and we certainly will not kill you. What did the king say to you?
45:26tell them, I am casting my appeal for mercy before the king’s eyes, not to send me back to Jonathan’s house to die there.
45:27All the rulers came to Jeremiah and questioned him. He reported everything the king had instructed him, and they fell silent, because the Lord’s word had not been heard.
45:28Jeremiah remained in the prison court until the time Jerusalem was captured.

46:16Go and tell Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: I am bringing My words upon this city for calamity, not good.

verses.text: 47:1The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah afterward, after Nebuzaradan, the chief guard from Daman, sent him away, when he took him in handcuffs among Judah’s exiles who were being led to Babylon.
47:2The chief guard took him and said to him, The Lord your God spoke these calamities against this place.
47:3And the Lord acted, because you sinned against Him and did not obey His voice.
47:4Behold, I have released you from the handcuffs on your hands. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you.

47:5But if not, go off and return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom Babylon’s king appointed in Judah’s land, and live with him among the people in Judah’s land. Go wherever it seems good in your eyes to go. The chief guard gave him gifts and sent him away.
47:6He came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and lived among the people left in the land.

47:7All the commanders of the force in the countryside, they and their men, heard that Babylon’s king had appointed Gedaliah in the land and had entrusted to him men and their wives whom he had not deported to Babylon.
47:8Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ophe the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite came to Gedaliah at Mizpah, they and their men.
47:9Gedaliah swore to them and their men, saying, Do not be afraid of the Chaldeans’ servants. Live in the land and work for Babylon’s king, and it will be better for you.

47:10Behold, I am staying before you at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who come against you. Gather wine and summer fruit, gather oil, put them in your containers, and live in the cities you have taken over.
47:11All the Judeans in Moab’s land, among Ammon’s people, in Idumea, and in all the land heard that Babylon’s king had left a remnant for Judah and appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over them.
47:12They came to Gedaliah in Judah’s land at Mizpah and gathered a very great amount of wine and summer fruit, and oil.
47:13Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the force in the countryside came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
47:14They said to him, Do you really know that Belisa king of Ammon’s people has sent Ishmael to you to take your life? But Gedaliah did not believe them.

47:15Johanan spoke secretly to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Let me go and strike down Ishmael, and let no one know, lest he take your life and all Judah gathered to you be scattered, and Judah’s survivors perish.
47:16Gedaliah said to Johanan, Do not do this thing, for you are speaking falsehoods about Ishmael.

verses.text: 48:1In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elasa, of the king’s family, came with ten men to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They ate bread together there.
48:2Ishmael and the ten men with him rose and struck Gedaliah, whom Babylon’s king had appointed over the land,
48:3and all the Judeans with him at Mizpah, and all the Chaldeans found there.
48:4On the second day after he struck Gedaliah, when no one knew,
48:5eighty men came from Shechem, Salem, and Samaria, with shaved beards and torn clothes, beating themselves, carrying grain offerings and frankincense to bring to the Lord’s house.
48:6Ishmael went out to meet them. They were walking and weeping, and he said to them, Come in to Gedaliah.
48:7When they entered the middle of the city, he slaughtered them into the cistern.
48:8Ten men found there said to Ishmael, Do not kill us, for we have stores in the countryside: wheat, barley, honey, and oil. He passed them by and did not kill them among their brothers.
48:9The cistern into which Ishmael threw all those he had struck down is a large cistern that King Asa made because of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael filled it with the slain.
48:10Ishmael turned back all the people left at Mizpah and the king’s daughters whom the chief guard had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, and he went away to the far side of Ammon’s people.
48:11Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the force with him heard of all the evils Ishmael had done.
48:12They led their entire army and went away to fight him. They found him beside abundant water at Gibeon.
48:13When all the people with Ishmael saw Johanan and the commanders of the force with him,
48:14they returned to Johanan.
48:15Ishmael escaped with eight men and went away to Ammon’s people.

48:16Johanan and all the commanders of the force with him took all the people left whom he had brought back from Ishmael: men mighty in war, the women, the rest, and the eunuchs whom he brought back from Gibeon.
48:17They went away and stayed at Gaberoth-chamaam near Bethlehem, intending to go into Egypt,
48:18away from the Chaldeans, for they feared them because Ishmael had struck Gedaliah, whom Babylon’s king had appointed in the land.

verses.text: 49:1All the commanders of the force, Johanan, Azariah son of Maaseiah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest, approached
49:2Jeremiah the prophet and said to him, Please let our appeal for mercy come before you. Pray to the Lord your God for these survivors, for few of us remain out of many, as your eyes see.
49:3Let the Lord your God tell us the way we should go and the matter we should carry out.
49:4Jeremiah said to them, I have heard. I will pray to the Lord our God as you have said. Whatever word the Lord answers, I will tell you; I certainly will not hide a word from you.
49:5They said to Jeremiah, May the Lord be a righteous and faithful witness among us if we do not act according to every word with which the Lord sends you to us.
49:6Whether good or bad, we will obey the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may be better for us, because we will obey the voice of the Lord our God.
49:7After ten days, the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah.
49:8He called Johanan, the commanders of the force, and all the people, from the least to the greatest.
49:9He said to them, Thus said the Lord:
49:10If you remain in this land, I will build you up and certainly not tear you down; I will plant you and certainly not pluck you up. For I have rested from the calamities I brought upon you.
49:11Do not fear Babylon’s king, whom you fear. Do not fear, says the Lord, for I am with you to rescue you and save you from his hand.

49:14because we will enter Egypt’s land, certainly not see war or hear the trumpet’s sound or hunger for bread, and there we will live—
49:15therefore hear the Lord’s word. Thus said the Lord: If you set your faces toward Egypt and go in to live there,
49:16the sword you fear will find you in Egypt’s land, and the famine you are concerned about will catch up with you from behind in Egypt, and there you will die.

49:17All the people and all the foreigners who set their faces toward Egypt’s land to live there will perish by sword and famine. None of them will be saved from the calamities I am bringing upon them.

49:18For thus said the Lord: As My wrath dripped upon Jerusalem’s inhabitants, so My wrath will drip upon you when you enter Egypt. You will become an untrodden place, subject to others, a curse, and a reproach, and you certainly will never see this place again.
49:19These are the things the Lord spoke concerning you, Judah’s survivors: Do not enter Egypt. And now know for certain

49:21And you did not obey the Lord’s voice, with which He sent me to you.
49:22And now you will perish by sword and famine in the place where you want to go and live.

verses.text: 51:1The word that came to Jeremiah for all the Judeans living in Egypt’s land and those staying at Migdol, Taphnas, and in Pathoures’s land:
51:2Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: You have seen all the calamities I brought upon Jerusalem and Judah’s cities. Behold, they are deserted of inhabitants,
51:3because of the wickedness they committed to embitter Me, going to burn incense to other gods whom you did not know.
51:4I sent you My servants the prophets at dawn, and I sent them saying, Do not commit this act of defilement that I hate.
51:5But they did not listen to Me or incline their ear to turn from their evils and stop burning incense to other gods.
51:6My anger and wrath dripped out and blazed in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem, and they became a desolation and an untrodden place, as on this day.

51:7Now thus said the Lord Almighty: Why are you doing great evils against yourselves, cutting off from yourselves man and woman, little child and nursing infant from Judah, so that none of you remains,

51:8embittering Me with the work of your hands by burning incense to other gods in Egypt’s land, which you entered to live there, so that you are cut off and become a curse and a reproach among all the earth’s nations?
51:9Have you forgotten your fathers’ evils, the evils of Judah’s kings, your rulers’ evils, and your wives’ evils, which they committed in Judah’s land and outside Jerusalem?
51:10They have not stopped to this day and have not held fast to My ordinances, which I set before their fathers.
51:11Therefore thus said the Lord: I am setting My face
51:12to destroy all the survivors in Egypt, and they will fall. By sword and famine they will perish, from the least to the greatest, and become a reproach, a destruction, and a curse.
51:13I will visit those staying in Egypt’s land as I visited Jerusalem, by sword, famine, and death.
51:14None of Judah’s remainder residing in Egypt’s land will be saved to return to Judah’s land, where they hope in their souls to return. They certainly will not return except those rescued.
51:15All the men who knew that their wives burned incense to other gods, all the women, a great assembly, and all the people staying in Egypt’s land at Pathoures answered Jeremiah:
51:16As for the word you spoke to us in the Lord’s name, we will not listen to you.

51:17We will certainly do everything that will come from our mouths: burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, as we, our fathers, our kings, and our rulers did in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem. We were filled with bread, were well off, and saw no calamities.
51:18But when we stopped burning incense to the queen of heaven, we were all diminished and perished by sword and famine.
51:19And when we burn incense to the queen of heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes for her and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands?
51:20Jeremiah said to all the people—to the mighty men, the women, and all the people who had answered him:

51:21Was it not the incense you burned in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem—you, your fathers, your kings, your rulers, and the people of the land—that the Lord remembered, and did it not come into His heart?
51:22The Lord could no longer bear the wickedness of your actions and the abominations you had committed. Your land became a desolation, an untrodden place, and a curse, as on this day,
51:23because you burned incense, sinned against the Lord, did not obey the Lord’s voice, and did not walk in His ordinances, law, and testimonies. These calamities have seized you.
51:24Jeremiah said to the people and the women, Hear the Lord’s word:

51:25Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: You women spoke with your mouths and fulfilled it with your hands, saying, We will certainly carry out our pledges that we pledged, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her. You firmly persisted in your pledges and indeed carried them out.

51:26Therefore hear the Lord’s word, all Judah staying in Egypt’s land: I have sworn by My great name, said the Lord, that My name will no longer be in any Judean’s mouth to say, As the Lord, the Lord, lives, throughout Egypt’s land.
51:27For I am watching over them to harm them, not do them good. All Judah living in Egypt’s land will perish by sword and famine until they perish.
51:28Those saved from the sword will return to Judah’s land, few in number. Judah’s survivors who settled in Egypt’s land to live there will know whose word will endure.
51:29This will be the sign for you that I will visit you for evils:

51:30Thus said the Lord: I am handing Ouaphre king of Egypt over to his enemy and those seeking his life, as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.
51:31The word Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when he wrote these words in the scroll from Jeremiah’s mouth, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah:
51:32Thus said the Lord concerning you, Baruch:
51:33For you said, Woe to me, woe to me! The Lord has added toil to my pain. I lay down amid groanings and found no rest.
51:34Tell him, Thus said the Lord: Those I have built up I am tearing down, and those I have planted I am plucking up.
51:35Are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them, for I am bringing calamities upon all flesh, says the Lord. I will give your life as gain wherever you walk.

verses.text: 52:1Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Amitaal daughter of Jeremiah, from Lobena.

52:4In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his force came against Jerusalem. They enclosed her with a palisade and built around her with squared stones.
52:5The city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
52:6On the ninth of the month, the famine grew severe in the city, and there were no loaves for the people of the land.

52:7The city was breached, and all the warriors went out at night by the gate between the wall and the outer wall beside the king’s garden, while the Chaldeans surrounded the city. They went by the road to Arabah,
52:8and the Chaldean force pursued the king and overtook him beyond Jericho. All his servants scattered away from him.
52:9They captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Deblatha, and he spoke to him in judgment.
52:10The king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, and he slaughtered all Judah’s rulers at Deblatha.
52:11He blinded Zedekiah’s eyes and bound him in fetters. The king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in a mill house until the day he died.
52:12In the fifth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuzaradan, the chief guard who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
52:13He burned the Lord’s house, the king’s house, and all the city’s houses; every great house he burned with fire.
52:14The Chaldean force with the chief guard pulled down the whole wall of Jerusalem all around.
52:16The chief guard left the remaining people as vinedressers and farmers.
52:17The Chaldeans shattered the bronze pillars in the Lord’s house, the bases, and the bronze Sea in the Lord’s house. They took their bronze and carried it to Babylon.
52:18And the rim, the bowls, the meat forks, and all the bronze utensils with which they performed service,
52:19and the saphphoth, the masmaroth, the pouring vessels, the lampstands, the incense bowls, and the ladles—those of gold, gold, and those of silver, silver—the chief guard took.
52:20The two pillars, the one Sea, and the twelve bronze calves beneath the Sea, which King Solomon made for the Lord’s house—their bronze was beyond weighing.
52:21As for the pillars, one pillar was thirty-five cubits high, and a cord of twelve cubits encircled it. Its thickness was four fingerbreadths all around,

52:22and a bronze cornice was on them. The projection of one cornice was five cubits in length, and a net and pomegranates surrounded the cornice, all of bronze. The second pillar had the same: eight pomegranates per cubit over the twelve cubits.
52:23There were ninety-six pomegranates on one side; all the pomegranates around the net numbered one hundred.
52:24The chief guard took the first priest, the second priest, and the three men guarding the road,

52:25and one eunuch who supervised the warriors, seven prominent men in the king’s presence who were found in the city, the scribe of the forces who kept records for the people of the land, and sixty people from the people of the land found inside the city.
52:26Nebuzaradan, the chief guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Deblatha,
52:27and the king of Babylon struck them at Deblatha in Aimath’s land.

52:31In the thirty-seventh year after Ioakim king of Judah had been deported, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fourth of the month, Oulaimaradach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, took up the head of Ioakim king of Judah and brought him out of the house where he was guarded.
52:32He spoke kindly to him and placed his throne above the thrones of the kings with him in Babylon.
52:33He changed his prison robe, and he ate bread continually before him all the days he lived.
52:34His allowance was given to him continually by the king of Babylon, from day to day until the day he died.

INTRODUCTION

Introducing Jeremiah

Jeremiah records the ministry of a prophet who warned Judah of coming judgement and lived to see Jerusalem fall. In the midst of disaster it promises a new covenant written on the heart.

SETTING
Jeremiah preached in Jerusalem during the last decades of Judah, through the Babylonian sieges and into the flight to Egypt.
AUTHOR
Traditionally attributed to Jeremiah, with his scribe Baruch recording his words. Scholars generally accept a core from Jeremiah, with later editing; the Greek version is notably shorter.
DATE
Jeremiah’s ministry c. 627–580 BC; final editing during or after the Exile.

Editorial guide

Read the editorial guide

Current Bespoke editorial guide

All 52 chapters, comprising 1296 existing verse units, have received the Bespoke English editorial pass: 568 revised and 728 retained. Source-specific numbering, names, repetitions and verse anchors are preserved. The newer Bespoke Saints English (1).pdf governs, with accepted Genesis 1–11 as the English benchmark. It supersedes the older Founding Style Guide where their pronoun rules conflict: Thou/Thee/Thy/Thine address God directly; ordinary address uses you/your.

Rahlfs–Hanhart 2006 remains the user-authorized provisional base. Focused checks of the publisher’s Greek running text are recorded by chapter. This is an English editorial revision, not a complete critical-text or apparatus verification. Göttingen, full apparatus, independent Greek and human read-aloud reviews remain pending. All English verse units were individually reviewed, and the full displayed Greek running text was read chapter by chapter with focused comparison of the recorded features. This does not constitute exhaustive critical-text verification.

The newer Bespoke PDF governs this reading edition. Saints Translation literal-smooth and all comparison/study streams remain separate and unchanged. Notes are separated from Scripture. Earlier source and wording notes are historical records and may quote superseded wording or pronouns; the dated current Bespoke notes explain this revision. The earlier editorial guide remains linked as a historical reference and does not override the newer PDF.

The existing Greek-based numbering, verse gaps and combined labels remain intact. The site places 23:7–8 after 23:6, although the consulted source displays them after 23:40. The combined site labels 25:13/32:13 and 25:14/25:20 are retained, including their existing placement. These layout differences are disclosed rather than silently rearranged. Historical lexical and comparative notes, footnote anchors, images and navigation are preserved.
